summary: The ten-year public-service digitalisation master plan [is in force](2023-05-10-pddsp-plan-directeur-digitalisation-services-publics-2023-2033) and its financing project [was reviewed at mid-term in March 2026](2026-03-23-pafen-evaluation-mi-parcours-transformation-numerique).
developments:
[The Plan directeur de digitalisation des services publics 2023-2033 was adopted in Council of Ministers on 10 May 2023](2023-05-10-pddsp-plan-directeur-digitalisation-services-publics-2023-2033) and is the country's standing digital transformation instrument.

2025-11 — [a high-level workshop under the Prime Minister's patronage turned the plan into an implementation roadmap](2025-11-15-atelier-echanges-economie-numerique-burundi) across administration digitalisation, connectivity, financial inclusion, innovation and cybersecurity.

2026-03 — [the World Bank conducted a mid-term review of the project financing that work](2026-03-23-pafen-evaluation-mi-parcours-transformation-numerique). What the base does not hold is any published progress measure against the plan: no service count, no target achieved, and no evaluation of the plan itself as distinct from the project funding it.

summary: The national ICT policy [ran to 2025 and has expired with no adopted successor](2011-07-13-pndtic-politique-nationale-developpement-tic-2010-2025); sector strategy is now to be written under a long-range vision instead.
developments:
[The Politique nationale de developpement des technologies de l'information et de la communication was adopted in Council of Ministers on 13 July 2011 for a term running to 2025](2011-07-13-pndtic-politique-nationale-developpement-tic-2010-2025). Its term has expired and no adopted successor was located.

2026-07-03 — [the Prime Minister instructed ministries to produce implementation documents for the Vision 2040-2060, with public-administration digitalisation and e-government among the first priority programmes](2026-07-04-primature-oriente-ministeres-vision-2040-2060). That is now the mechanism by which sector ICT strategy is to be written, and it is a process rather than a strategy: no document, timetable or budget is published.

progress: Mixed, a strategy still unadopted while a mapping system was built
summary: A national broadband strategy [was validated in 2017 and never adopted](2018-03-01-arct-rapport-annuel-2017-burundi-large-bande-2025), while a [broadband mapping system was established in late 2025](2025-12-04-africa-bb-maps-rapport-evenement-national-cartographie-large-bande-burundi).
developments:
[Burundi Large Bande 2025 was drawn up with technical-union support and validated by stakeholders on 6 December 2017, and was still awaiting government adoption](2018-03-01-arct-rapport-annuel-2017-burundi-large-bande-2025). No published full text and no adopting act were located, so a strategy named after a year that has now passed has never been in force.

2025-10-28 to 30 — [a national event established a broadband mapping system under regulator stewardship, to identify underserved areas, direct investment and support an operational roadmap](2025-12-04-africa-bb-maps-rapport-evenement-national-cartographie-large-bande-burundi). Mapping where coverage is absent is the input a broadband strategy would use; the strategy it would feed is the one that has not been adopted.

progress: Advanced, a strategy pillar with no build behind it
summary: A sovereign cloud and data hubs [are a pillar of the AI strategy, built around a planned data centre](2026-04-23-burundi-six-pillar-ai-strategy-wearetech), with no build on record.
developments:
[A sovereign cloud and national data hubs are one of the six pillars of the April 2026 artificial-intelligence strategy, framed around the state technology agency's data centre](2026-04-23-burundi-six-pillar-ai-strategy-wearetech). Nothing existed before it and nothing has been built since.

The data centre itself is reported under data storage and remains a stated priority with no site or date. So the country has a cloud policy, a data governance strategy and a data protection statute, and no national facility for any of them to run on.

summary: A cross-government information-systems concept [was presented for validation in December 2024](2024-12-17-setic-concept-type-systemes-information-institutions-publiques) as the route to adopting international ICT standards.
developments:
2024-12-17 — [the state technology secretariat presented the final Concept type des systemes d'information des institutions publiques to stakeholders for validation, described as a foundation of digitalisation permitting the adoption of international ICT standards](2024-12-17-setic-concept-type-systemes-information-institutions-publiques).

What the record shows is presentation for validation, not formal adoption. No published text, adopting instrument, technical specification or compliance obligation on ministries is held, so the base can date the document and cannot say what it requires of any institution.

summary: A National AI Strategy for 2026 to 2030 [was validated in April 2026 on six pillars](2026-04-23-burundi-six-pillar-ai-strategy-wearetech), including a sovereign cloud and about fifteen health and agriculture pilots.
developments:
2026-04-22 — [the strategy was validated on six pillars: governance and ethics, sovereign cloud and data hubs, education and research, innovation and incubators, human capital, and about fifteen health and agriculture pilots](2026-04-23-burundi-six-pillar-ai-strategy-wearetech), and [it was presented as the centre of the country's digital strategy](2026-04-22-lia-au-coeur-de-la-strategie-numerique-burundi). It sets a target of training more than a thousand officials.

It follows [a national readiness diagnostic run in November 2025](2025-11-25-atelier-national-paysage-intelligence-artificielle-burundi). No implementing decree, budget line or first pilot has been reported since validation, and the compute the strategy assumes does not exist: no source on this ledger states any national computing capacity.

summary: A regional regulatory profile [records no national framework on cross-border data transfers and no measure restricting them](2024-01-04-uneca-atpc-digital-trade-regulatory-integration-country-profile-burundi).
developments:
[The digital trade regulatory profile states that Burundi has no national legal framework on cross-border transfers of data and no measures restricting them, including on the location of data, local storage, bans on data transfers or local processing requirements](2024-01-04-uneca-atpc-digital-trade-regulatory-integration-country-profile-burundi).

The finding is a stated absence rather than a gap in the record, which is the more useful of the two. Two caveats travel with it: the profile carries no printed publication date and its underlying regulatory survey runs only to December 2021, and the personal data protection law promulgated in March 2026 is an image-only scan, so whether it introduced a transfer or localisation rule cannot be read from the base.

summary: A National Data Governance Strategy [was validated in November 2025 on seven pillars](2025-11-14-burundi-adopts-national-data-governance-strategy), treating data as a public good.
developments:
2025-11-14 — [a National Data Governance Strategy was validated on seven pillars, supported by the United Nations regional commission and aligned to the African Union data policy framework, treating data as a public good](2025-11-14-burundi-adopts-national-data-governance-strategy). None existed before it.

Validation is not adoption: no decree, gazettal or implementing instrument appears on the ledger in the nine months since, and no institution is named as owning the strategy. The data protection law reported under legislation arrived two months later and is the only binding instrument on this ground.

summary: A draft access-to-information law [was adopted in Council of Ministers on 10 June 2026](2026-06-13-conseil-ministres-adopte-projet-loi-acces-information-publique); no open-data policy instrument is held.
developments:
2026-06-10 — [the Council of Ministers adopted the draft law on access to public information, presented by the communication and media minister](2026-06-13-conseil-ministres-adopte-projet-loi-acces-information-publique). It is a draft adopted in Council rather than a law in force: no text is published and no parliamentary date is set.

Against it the base holds no national open-data policy or strategy. What exists is an operative licence rather than a policy: [the statistics institute publishes an open licence governing reuse of the data on its own platform](2025-06-10-insbu-accord-de-licence-ouverte-plateforme-donnees-ouvertes), which is an instrument of one institution and not a whole-of-government mandate.

summary: A personal data protection law [was unanimously adopted on 15 January 2026](2026-01-16-burundi-personal-data-protection-law-techafricanews): eight chapters, an independent authority and criminal penalties, where no statute existed.
developments:
2026-01-15 — the National Assembly [unanimously adopted a personal data protection law with eight chapters, an independent supervisory authority and criminal penalties, aligned to the African Union convention](2026-01-16-burundi-personal-data-protection-law-techafricanews), [reported the following day as the country's first such statute](2026-01-16 Burundi adopts data protection law). No statute existed before it.

The sequencing is stated by the government itself: legislation came first in order to enable the biometric identity card, which is reported under digital identity and is technically ready but waiting on its own instrument. The authority the law creates is not on record as operating, reported below.

summary: A stand-alone cybercrime statute [has been in force since March 2022](2022-03-16-loi-1-10-cybercriminalite), with cybersecurity obligations carried in the [2024 communications code](2024-08-22-loi-1-22-code-communications-electroniques-postales).
developments:
[Loi n 1/10 du 16 mars 2022 portant prevention et repression de la cybercriminalite is in force and recorded as such on the official legal database](2022-03-16-loi-1-10-cybercriminalite), and the base holds its complete promulgated text.

[The 2024 code des communications electroniques et postales carries cybersecurity obligations at articles 160 to 167 alongside it](2024-08-22-loi-1-22-code-communications-electroniques-postales). Nothing moved on either in the window. What the base does not hold is any implementing regulation, any national cybersecurity strategy, or any published enforcement action under the 2022 statute.

summary: A ministerial ordinance [made identity-card registration of every SIM compulsory from 25 June 2026](2026-06-05-ecofin-burundi-identification-cartes-sim-obligatoire), while the [identification file itself still awaits instituting texts](2026-01-01-isoko-fichier-national-identification-carte-nationale-identite).
developments:
2026-06 — [the regulator required every subscriber to regularise SIM identification against the national identity card, with non-compliant lines deactivated from 25 June 2026](2026-06-05-ecofin-burundi-identification-cartes-sim-obligatoire), under a ministerial ordinance of 13 January 2026. It is the first instrument on the ledger to make the national identity card a condition of holding a service.

Underneath it the register is not yet constituted: [the official procedure page for the Fichier National d'Identification states that further texts remain to be adopted to institute the file](2026-01-01-isoko-fichier-national-identification-carte-nationale-identite). An obligation to identify against a register precedes the instrument establishing the register.

summary: The 2018 payment-systems statute [is the framework law](2018-05-11-loi-1-07-systeme-national-paiement); the central bank has since published [an oversight framework](2025-11-20-brb-cadre-surveillance-paiement) and [launched a national instant payment system](2026-04-23-brb-lancement-burundipay).
developments:
[Loi n 1/07 du 11 mai 2018 portant systeme national de paiement is the framework statute, and the law the central bank cites for its power to regulate the issue and use of payment instruments; its articles 22 to 24 carry the move of payment instruments off paper and the admissibility of electronic and optical evidence](2018-05-11-loi-1-07-systeme-national-paiement). Every official copy located is an image-only scan.

[The central bank has published an oversight framework covering the real-time gross settlement system, the clearing house, the central securities depository, the national switch, instant payment systems and electronic money platforms, with a licensing, monitoring, inspection and sanction regime for payment service providers](2025-11-20-brb-cadre-surveillance-paiement), and in April 2026 [launched the national instant payment system under a regulation of its own](2026-04-23-brb-lancement-burundipay).

summary: A 2018 presidential decree [is the closest instrument to legislation enabling data sharing between public bodies](2018-07-25-decret-100-085-cadre-national-donnees); nothing moved on it.
developments:
[Decret n 100/085 du 25 juillet 2018 establishes the national framework for the collection, dissemination, access, archiving and security of data and micro-data](2018-07-25-decret-100-085-cadre-national-donnees). It defines administrative data as data collected by public institutions in the exercise of their functions, brings administrative data into the dissemination regime, and provides for making data available by electronic means, with institutional public users and rules on access.

It is an enabling instrument rather than a mandate: it does not require any two public bodies to connect, and the base holds no implementing text, no data-sharing agreement made under it and no platform operating on its authority.

summary: No binding artificial-intelligence instrument was located in any national legal source; [a non-binding strategy was validated in April 2026](2026-04-22-abp-validation-strategie-nationale-ia).
developments:
[No Burundian loi, decret, ordonnance ministerielle or regulator reglement governing artificial intelligence was located across the official legal database, the official gazette, the presidency, both chambers, the communications regulator and the state technology secretariat](2025-11-28-pnud-burundi-feuille-route-ia), on a search dated to the national readiness assessment held in Bujumbura on 25-27 November 2025.

2026-04-21 — [a national validation session for the artificial-intelligence strategy was opened by the ministry responsible for the digital economy with a development agency](2026-04-22-abp-validation-strategie-nationale-ia). What moved is the validation of a non-binding strategy, not any instrument: the absence the indicator asks about is unchanged and is now dated.

summary: There is no free-standing e-commerce statute; coverage sits in the [2024 communications code](2024-08-22-loi-1-22-code-communications-electroniques-postales), under which the regulator [made a conformity declaration compulsory in June 2026](2026-06-26-arct-declaration-conformite-commerce-electronique).
developments:
[There is no Burundian law on electronic commerce, electronic transactions or electronic signature; coverage is carried inside the 2024 code des communications electroniques et postales, whose article 1 applies to all transactions by electronic means](2024-08-22-loi-1-22-code-communications-electroniques-postales), and the regulator treats that code as the legal basis for electronic commerce.

2026-05-29 — [the regulator published guidelines for the national electronic-commerce sector setting technical, operational and organisational standards for interoperability, transparency, transaction security and online consumer protection](2026-05-29-arct-lignes-directrices-ecosysteme-commerce-electronique).

2026-06-26 — [it then made a prior conformity declaration compulsory for platforms and merchant sites operating in Burundi](2026-06-26-arct-declaration-conformite-commerce-electronique), which is the operative regulatory step. The guidelines themselves are an image-only scan, so what they require cannot be read from the base.

summary: Statistics legislation [is a chain of three acts rather than a code](2021-05-20-loi-1-08-organisation-systeme-statistique), the 2021 recast being the most recent link with a machine-readable text.
developments:
[Loi n 1/08 du 20 mai 2021 recast the 2007 law organising the national statistical system](2021-05-20-loi-1-08-organisation-systeme-statistique), and is the substantive recast in a chain running from the 2007 statute through this one to a further modification of 24 July 2023 that the statistics institute cites as the governing law.

No gazetted text of the 2023 modification was located, so the operative law can be named and its current wording cannot be read. Nothing moved on the statute in the window.

summary: An access to information bill [was listed on the National Assembly's order paper for the session opened on 3 August 2026](2026-08-04-burundi-national-assembly-august-session-access-to-information-bill), with no text published.
developments:
2026-08-04 — [the bill was listed for examination in the session opened on 3 August 2026](2026-08-04-burundi-national-assembly-august-session-access-to-information-bill). No text, tabling number, sponsoring ministry or timetable has been published, and none existed before this listing.

The session runs about three months under the constitution, which is the outer bound for passage in this sitting. Nothing else on this ledger touches access to information: there is no open data portal, no open data policy and no published dataset, so the bill would arrive into an absence rather than onto a practice.

summary: The data protection authority [was created by the January 2026 law](2026-01-16-burundi-personal-data-protection-law-techafricanews), with no appointment, budget or decision on file since.
developments:
[The January 2026 data protection law provides for an independent supervisory authority](2026-01-16-burundi-personal-data-protection-law-techafricanews). Seven months on, no appointment, budget, seat or decision appears on the record, so the body exists in statute and not in operation.

That gap matters here more than usual. The biometric identity card, the digital civil registry and the instant payment system are all being built inside the same period, and the authority that would supervise their processing has not been constituted. The only consumer-facing enforcement on this ledger came from the telecommunications regulator instead, reported under payments consumer protection.

summary: A first personal data protection law [was promulgated on 10 March 2026](2026-03-10-loi-1-03-2026-protection-donnees-caractere-personnel), replacing a position in which [no legal regime for personal data existed](2025-10-22-conseil-ministres-communique-11-2025).
developments:
2025-10-22 — [the Council of Ministers adopted the draft law, recording the government's own position that the collection and processing of personal data in Burundi had no legal framework or regime at that date](2025-10-22-conseil-ministres-communique-11-2025).

2026-01-15 — [the National Assembly adopted the bill unanimously in plenary](2026-01-30-assemblee-adoption-loi-protection-donnees), the same account recording that the biometric national identity card process was under way in twelve pilot zones.

2026-03-10 — [Loi n 1/03 was promulgated and published by the regulator on 18 March](2026-03-10-loi-1-03-2026-protection-donnees-caractere-personnel). The official text is an image-only scan with no text layer, so the base can state that a law exists and cannot yet state what it requires — including whether it carries any cross-border transfer or localisation rule. No supervisory authority, commencement date or implementing regulation is held.

summary: Burundi [joined the regional One Network Area and ratified the digital integration protocol](2025-01-21-burundi-embraces-eac-digital-integration-ict-growth), and [agreed a continental trade implementation roadmap in August 2026](2026-08-06-afcfta-secretary-general-begins-official-mission-to-burundi).
developments:
2025-01-21 — [the country joined the East African One Network Area and ratified the regional digital integration protocol](2025-01-21-burundi-embraces-eac-digital-integration-ict-growth), where neither applied before.

2026-08-03 — [a technical team agreed during a continental trade secretariat mission to produce a country profile and implementation roadmap jointly owned by government and the private sector](2026-08-06-afcfta-secretary-general-begins-official-mission-to-burundi), tied by the minister to the country's African Union chairmanship, with the adjustment fund discussed as a financing route. No roadmap, profile or timetable has been published.

2026-07-28 — separately, [a telecommunications-technology memorandum with Vietnam reached an implementation meeting, party to party rather than ministry to ministry](2026-07-28-burundi-vietnam-digital-transformation-cooperation), producing policy transfer, equipment and scholarships and no monetary commitment, against [a memorandum signed in November 2024 with no digital follow-through reported](2024-11-20-vietnam-burundi-mou-telecom-technology).

summary: The regional assembly [endorsed a bill creating an East African statistics bureau, with Burundian amendments](2025-10-10-eala-endorses-eac-regional-statistics-bureau); the bureau is not on record as established.
developments:
2025-10-10 — [the East African Legislative Assembly endorsed the bill establishing a regional statistics bureau, carrying amendments from Burundi](2025-10-10-eala-endorses-eac-regional-statistics-bureau). Nothing existed before it and the bureau is not on record as constituted.

It is the only regional legal instrument on this ledger that Burundi shaped rather than joined. The two others — the One Network Area and the digital integration protocol — were acceded to as drafted, and the cross-border data-sharing framework reported below was validated regionally with no national implementing instrument since.

summary: Submarine access [runs through neighbouring countries with cross-border fibre interconnection](2021-07-01-arct-rapport-indicateurs-tic-burundi-edition-2020), and a [regional roaming framework is under development](2026-05-25-eac-regional-mobile-roaming-framework-development).
developments:
[The regulator's own indicators report brings the position together: submarine cable access to EASSy, SEACOM and TEAMS through neighbouring countries, national backbone cross-border interconnection points with Rwanda, the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Tanzania, and regional roaming](2021-07-01-arct-rapport-indicateurs-tic-burundi-edition-2020). A landlocked country's international capacity is its neighbours' landings, and that is what this row records.

2026-05-25 to 29 — [regional engagements opened development of a harmonised regional mobile roaming framework under the single digital market agenda](2026-05-25-eac-regional-mobile-roaming-framework-development), a framework-development milestone rather than an adopted tariff.

2026-06-23 to 24 — [Burundi endorsed shared regional digital infrastructure, harmonised data-exchange frameworks and digital trust for interoperable cross-border public services at the regional development forum](2026-06-26-burundi-marche-unique-numerique-afrique-est-eac-d4d-forum).

summary: A regional secure data-sharing framework [was validated in June 2026](2026-06-25-eac-backs-secure-data-sharing-framework) under the East Africa digital integration project, with no national implementing instrument.
developments:
2026-06-25 — [an East African cross-border secure data-sharing framework was validated under the regional digital integration project](2026-06-25-eac-backs-secure-data-sharing-framework), where none existed before.

No national implementing instrument is on file. The domestic law that would carry it is four months older — the January 2026 data protection statute — and its supervisory authority is not operating, so the country has agreed a regional transfer framework before constituting the body that would administer transfers under it.

summary: Health standards [were defined at a national workshop in April 2026](2026-04-13-burundi-systeme-information-sante-interoperable-hl7-fhir) and the education system [was assessed against continental norms in June](2026-06-09-au-iped-supports-burundi-strengthening-education-data); no cross-government standard is adopted.
developments:
2026-04-07 to 10 — [a national health information workshop defined common technical standards, naming HL7 FHIR, with priority data-exchange flows and mediation for the country's fragmented health platforms](2026-04-13-burundi-systeme-information-sante-interoperable-hl7-fhir).

2026-06 — [Burundi self-assessed its education management information system against the continental EMIS norms and standards at a three-day technical workshop](2026-06-09-au-iped-supports-burundi-strengthening-education-data); no score or action plan is published.

Both are sectoral. The cross-government instrument that would sit above them, [the Concept type des systemes d'information des institutions publiques, was presented for validation in December 2024](2024-12-17-setic-concept-type-systemes-information-institutions-publiques) and has not been adopted.

summary: A national quality policy [was adopted in February 2022](2022-02-02-conseil-ministres-02-fevrier-2022-politique-nationale-qualite), and the standards bureau [signed a mutual-recognition protocol with a neighbour in August 2025](2025-09-01-protocole-occ-bbn-normalisation-controle-qualite-certification).
developments:
2022-02-02 — [the Council of Ministers adopted the Politique Nationale Qualite as the government's base instrument for establishing and supervising the national quality infrastructure system, setting its objectives, roadmap and timetable](2022-02-02-conseil-ministres-02-fevrier-2022-politique-nationale-qualite). The policy text itself is not held.

2025-08-29 — [the standards and quality control bureau signed a memorandum with the Congolese control office covering exchange of information on standards and quality assurance, metrology, conformity assessment and pre- and post-shipment inspection, with progressive mutual recognition of conformity certificates](2025-09-01-protocole-occ-bbn-normalisation-controle-qualite-certification). No official page carrying the protocol was located, so it is held through trade press.

summary: [628 of 690 harmonised regional standards are adopted, 91 per cent](2023-06-01-eac-partner-states-harmonized-standards-adoption-status-june-2023), and the payment system [migrated to ISO 20022 in February 2026](2026-02-05-brb-migration-ats-norme-iso-20022).
developments:
[Burundi has adopted 628 of 690 harmonised East African standards and not adopted 62, a rate of 91 per cent and the highest of the six partner states](2023-06-01-eac-partner-states-harmonized-standards-adoption-status-june-2023), on a catalogue drawing on international standards among others. It is a first count with no earlier figure behind it, so the level is stated and the direction is not.

2026-02-05 — [the central bank completed migration of the national automated transfer system to ISO 20022, with interbank operations resuming on the new system the following day, stated to ease integration with regional and international payment and settlement systems](2026-02-05-brb-migration-ats-norme-iso-20022). It is the clearest instance on this ledger of an international standard being adopted into a working national system rather than into a catalogue.

summary: A consumer association [called for a national convention on communications](2026-07-31-burundi-abuco-denounces-telecom-service-degradation) after denouncing service degradation, with no response from government or operators on file.
developments:
2026-07-31 — [the consumer association denounced degradation of telecommunications service and proposed a national convention on communications](2026-07-31-burundi-abuco-denounces-telecom-service-degradation). No convening date, government response or operator response is on file.

It is the only non-governmental intervention in digital policy this ledger records. The same association is behind the tariff account reported under affordability, and the regulator's injunctions on value-added services followed its complaints — so the one civil-society actor visible in the record is a consumer body acting on billing rather than a research or advocacy sector engaging with strategy.

progress: Mixed, a first multi-stakeholder forum against two decades of documented controls
summary: Burundi [hosted a regional internet governance forum for the first time in February 2026](2026-02-19-burundi-accueille-forum-gouvernance-internet-afrique-centrale), against [two decades of documented internet controls](2020-01-01-cipesa-state-of-internet-freedom-burundi-2019).
developments:
[A civil-society study mapping government internet controls from 1999 to 2019 records surveillance, restrictive media regulation, censorship of a named outlet and civil-society resistance](2020-01-01-cipesa-state-of-internet-freedom-burundi-2019). Its evidence base stops in 2019 and it is not a current snapshot.

2026-02-16 to 21 — [Burundi hosted the Central Africa Internet Governance Forum for the first time, with eleven countries and government, youth, women, private-sector and technical participants, validating a 2026 regional roadmap](2026-02-19-burundi-accueille-forum-gouvernance-internet-afrique-centrale). It is the clearest instance of open multi-stakeholder discussion of digital policy the base holds for the country. What it is not is evidence of domestic consultation on a domestic instrument: none of the strategies or laws in this chapter was published in draft for comment.

progress: Mixed, the ICT vote tripled and a first domestic identity line appeared while whole-budget revenue realisation fell short
summary: The ICT ministry vote [rose to BIF 131.7bn](2026-05-13-le-renouveau-loi-reglement-compte-rendu-budgetaire-2024-2025) and [BIF 16.0bn was proposed for the identity card](2026-06-11-bdi-2026-cni-biometrique), against [76.79% revenue realisation](2026-05-13-le-renouveau-loi-reglement-compte-rendu-budgetaire-2024-2025).
developments:
2026-05-13 — the settlement law [put the communications and ICT ministry vote at BIF 131.7bn for 2024/25 against BIF 43.1bn the year before](2026-05-13-le-renouveau-loi-reglement-compte-rendu-budgetaire-2024-2025). The same instrument [records whole-budget revenue realised at BIF 3,234bn, 76.79% of a revised target that had itself been cut from BIF 5,076bn to BIF 4,732bn](2026-05-13-le-renouveau-loi-reglement-compte-rendu-budgetaire-2024-2025).

2026-06-11 — [BIF 16.0bn was proposed in the draft 2026/27 budget for the biometric identity card](2026-06-11-bdi-2026-cni-biometrique), the first domestic state digital line this base tracks for the country. [A universal service fund appropriation of BIF 11.40bn was revised in for dedicated transit to health facilities and schools](2026-07-01-bdi-2026-fsu-connectivite-institutions), on an own-source levy.

The reason a voted line is not a spent line is on the record: [a mid-year work plan showed credits shifted between programmes with a 2.7% overrun](2025-10-27-burundi-eco-budget-2024-2025-urgences-ptba-s2), and [the 2026/27 budget was adopted with expenditure above BIF 7,020bn against revenue of BIF 6,296.03bn, with the audit court telling senators it lacked clarity on remaining public debt](2026-06-19-burundi-eco-budget-general-2026-2027-adopte-cour-des-comptes).

summary: A five-year health-sector memorandum with the United States [commits US$156m and covers health-data management](2026-02-09-us-commits-156m-burundi-health-sector-agreement).
developments:
2026-02-09 — [a five-year agreement with the United States committing US$156m to the health sector was signed, including health-data management](2026-02-09-us-commits-156m-burundi-health-sector-agreement). Nothing comparable existed before it and it is the largest single commitment on this ledger.

What it does not carry is a data instrument. No data-sharing agreement under the memorandum has been published, so the terms on which health data would move between the two parties are not on the record — at a point when the country's data protection authority has not been constituted.

summary: Two co-financed rural connectivity contracts were signed, [USD 10 million split 44:56 with an operator](2026-03-03-setic-pafen-lumitel-connectivite-4g-milieu-rural) and [USD 5,907,000 to serve 92 collines](2026-04-29-pafen-onatel-couverture-reseau-connectivite-milieu-rural).
developments:
2025-12 — [an operator was stated to have decided to double its investment to meet customer demand](2025-12-18-le-renouveau-premier-ministre-delegation-viettel), with no absolute amount and no baseline published, so what that evidences is a commercial commitment rather than a measured sum.

2026-03-03 — [a USD 10 million contract was signed to extend 4G broadband in rural areas, co-financed 44 per cent by government through the national project and 56 per cent by the operator](2026-03-03-setic-pafen-lumitel-connectivite-4g-milieu-rural).

2026-04-29 — [a USD 5,907,000 contract was signed to serve 92 collines with no 2G or 3G coverage, benefiting 372,035 people including schools and health facilities](2026-04-29-pafen-onatel-couverture-reseau-connectivite-milieu-rural). Both are the same instrument: public money buying commercial coverage where the commercial case does not stand on its own.

summary: The World Bank digital foundations project [reached 61% commitment at its mid-term review](2026-03-27-world-bank-reviews-burundi-pafen-reform-program), prioritising public-finance modernisation, the identity card and a data centre.
developments:
2026-03-27 — [the mid-term review put commitment at 61%, with priorities named as public-finance modernisation, the national identity card and a national data centre](2026-03-27-world-bank-reviews-burundi-pafen-reform-program), against [a project already under implementation](2026-01-01-world-bank-bdi-2026-burundi-pafen-lumitel-bw09).

It is the only development-partner digital financing on this ledger, and most of what moved in the window sits under it: the rural network contracts reported under mobile coverage, the mast programme, the broadband coverage target and the data centre that has not been built. No disbursement figure, results framework or restructuring is published, so commitment is the only measure available.

progress: Advanced, on contracted coverage rather than on any measured subscriber base
summary: Two operators [were contracted to build 4G on 178 hills](2026-05-05-onatel-5-9m-deal-digital-access-rural-burundi), a third [was licensed with no launch](2026-03-02-lyca-mobile-telecom-ehealth-burundi), and no national penetration figure exists.
developments:
2026-03-04 — [one operator was contracted at more than US$10m for 86 hills across 14 provinces](2026-03-04-lumitel-burundi-10m-high-speed-internet-project), and 2026-05-04 — [the incumbent for 92 hills at US$5.9m, stated to cover 372,035 people](2026-05-04-burundi-5-9m-contract-rural-network-techafricanews), [confirmed the following day](2026-05-05-onatel-5-9m-deal-digital-access-rural-burundi). [A mast-deployment programme under the same financing is named by the regulator as in train, addressing coverage rather than outages](2026-08-03-telecommunications-un-casse-tete-pour-les-abonnes).

2026-03-02 — [a third operator holds a licence granted in October 2025 with telecommunications and e-health plans and no service launch on file](2026-03-02-lyca-mobile-telecom-ehealth-burundi).

[An infrastructure-sharing law is named by the regulator as in draft, with no text, tabling date or sponsoring ministry published](2026-08-03-telecommunications-un-casse-tete-pour-les-abonnes). No subscriber total, penetration rate or regulator return appears anywhere on this ledger, so coverage contracts are visible and take-up is not.

summary: [12.5 per cent of Burundians were using the internet in early 2025](2026-02-28-abp-quand-la-5g-arrive-avant-la-3g-fonctionnelle), while a fifth-generation network launched commercially in December.
developments:
[The regulator's coverage figures put 3G at 50 to 54 per cent of the population, 4G at 32 to 34 per cent and 2G at 97 per cent, with only 12.5 per cent of Burundians actually using the internet in early 2025](2026-02-28-abp-quand-la-5g-arrive-avant-la-3g-fonctionnelle), against 80 installed fifth-generation sites after a commercial launch in December 2025. A separate account [cites international union data that nearly 90 per cent of Burundians had no internet access in 2023](2026-03-01-abp-burundi-etendre-4g-zones-rurales).

[The regulator publishes a quarterly market observatory covering voice, SMS, internet and mobile financial services, its fourth-quarter 2025 edition appearing in April 2026](2026-04-27-arct-observatoire-marche-tic-q4-2025) — the standing subscription-based series the indicator would be read from. Coverage and use are the gap this row records: a network reaching most of the population that most of the population does not use.

summary: Internet package tariffs [have more than doubled since January 2025, in some cases tripling](2026-07-31-burundi-abuco-denounces-telecom-service-degradation), on the consumer association's account.
developments:
2026-07-31 — [the consumer association reported that internet package tariffs have more than doubled since January 2025, in some cases doubling or tripling, alongside degradation of service](2026-07-31-burundi-abuco-denounces-telecom-service-degradation).

The account is the association's own. No regulator tariff series, operator price schedule or basket measure appears anywhere on this ledger, so the direction is reported by the party least likely to understate it and there is nothing to test it against.

Read beside it, the satellite alternative is also out of reach on cost, reported under satellite broadband, and the network people are paying more for is the one the regulator itself describes as degraded.

summary: [1,750 km on the national backbone covers all provinces](2025-08-27-arct-rapport-indicateurs-tic-burundi-edition-2024), with the regulator stating the national territory is now covered by fibre.
developments:
[Regulator statistics as at 31 December 2024 give fibre deployment by infrastructure operator: 1,750 km on the national backbone covering all provinces, 350 km of metropolitan network in the capital and 3,400 km on a third operator's network, and state that the national territory is now covered by fibre optic](2025-08-27-arct-rapport-indicateurs-tic-burundi-edition-2024).

2026-04 — [a presidential decree appointed a new director general of the mixed-economy company holding the backbone concession](2026-04-27-decret-100-055-nomination-dg-bbs), and [a second decree four days later named the administrators representing the state on its board](2026-04-27-decret-100-058-nomination-administrateurs-bbs). Governance moved; no traffic, utilisation or wholesale-price figure for the backbone is published, so what the fibre carries cannot be read from the base.

summary: International capacity [runs through neighbouring countries' submarine landings](2021-07-01-arct-rapport-indicateurs-tic-burundi-edition-2020); no capacity figure is published.
developments:
[The regulator's indicators report records submarine cable access to EASSy, SEACOM and TEAMS through neighbouring countries, cross-border fibre interconnection points with Rwanda, the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Tanzania, and regional roaming](2021-07-01-arct-rapport-indicateurs-tic-burundi-edition-2020).

For a landlocked country the international bandwidth position is its neighbours' landings and the transit bought over them. What the base does not hold is any capacity figure in Gbps, any wholesale transit price, or any statement of redundancy — which is the part that matters, since a single cross-border route is a single point of failure for the whole country's international traffic.

summary: A national internet exchange point [was created by decree in May 2014](2014-05-13-decret-100-122-cadre-reglementaire-point-echange-internet-national-burundi), its first objective keeping local traffic off international links.
developments:
[Decret n 100/122 du 13 mai 2014 creates the national internet exchange point as an exchange belonging to the Republic; article 2 sets its objectives, first among them keeping local traffic off international links, and article 3 places its management with an internet service provider association chosen and authorised by the regulator](2014-05-13-decret-100-122-cadre-reglementaire-point-echange-internet-national-burundi).

The founding instrument is held and the operating record is not: no traffic figure, member count, uptime statement or annual report for the exchange was located, so the base can say the exchange exists in law and cannot say whether it carries anything.

summary: Satellite broadband [is licensed but effectively unavailable on cost, the kit alone at roughly US$500](2025-09-10-unreliable-connectivity-impacts-burundi-citizens), unchanged through the window.
developments:
[The service is licensed and effectively unavailable on price, with the terminal alone at roughly US$500](2025-09-10-unreliable-connectivity-impacts-burundi-citizens). That was the position at the start of the window and nothing has moved it since: no tariff change, no subscriber figure, no second satellite operator and no regulatory statement appears.

It is the only alternative to a mobile network that the regulator describes as failing mainly on electricity, and it is priced beyond the population it would serve. No universal-service subsidy, terminal financing or institutional purchase of satellite capacity is on the ledger.

summary: [No shared government data centre exists](2020-01-01-world-bank-burundi-digital-economy-assessment) and capacity is being added one agency at a time, a development agency [tendering for its own racks](2026-02-18-adb-appel-offres-racks-data-center-stabilisateurs-projecteurs).
developments:
[A country diagnostic records that no shared government data centre exists, that the revenue office, the central bank and the presidency each run their own, that the backbone company hosts a national data centre other public agencies use for backup, that it operates one level-3 data centre built for USD 2 million, and that there are only about four data centres of decent grade in the country](2020-01-01-world-bank-burundi-digital-economy-assessment).

2026-02 — [a development agency published a full national open tender for data centre racks, stabilisers and projectors with technical specifications and quantities](2026-02-18-adb-appel-offres-racks-data-center-stabilisateurs-projecteurs). It is concrete in-window procurement of physical capacity, and it is for one agency's own facility rather than for a national one — which is the pattern the diagnostic described six years earlier and nothing since has changed.

summary: A national data centre [is named a mid-term priority of the World Bank programme](2026-03-27-world-bank-reviews-burundi-pafen-reform-program), with no build, site or date on file.
developments:
[The data centre is named as a mid-term priority alongside public-finance modernisation and the national identity card](2026-03-27-world-bank-reviews-burundi-pafen-reform-program). No build, site, capacity or date appears, and no baseline was held before it.

It is the only data centre of any kind on this ledger — no commercial facility, no colocation provider and no hosting arrangement is recorded for the country. The sovereign cloud pillar of the artificial-intelligence strategy is built around this facility, so a strategy adopted in April 2026 depends on a building that has not been started.

summary: The central bank [maintains a physically separate alternative site](2025-11-19-brb-appel-offres-maintenance-site-alternatif-rumonge), and the state technology body [is procuring virtualisation and backup equipment](2026-04-08-pafen-aao-equipements-additionnels-setic-virtualisation-backup).
developments:
2025-11-19 — [the central bank issued an international tender for maintenance works on its alternative site, financed from its own funds](2025-11-19-brb-appel-offres-maintenance-site-alternatif-rumonge). It is the clearest evidence that a physically separate secondary site for continuity of critical systems exists and is being maintained rather than left dormant; the notice covers building works and states no IT capacity, rack count or replication arrangement.

2026-04 — [a re-issued tender sought additional equipment and licences for virtualisation and backup at the state technology secretariat](2026-04-08-pafen-aao-equipements-additionnels-setic-virtualisation-backup), the body hosting national platforms. Backup capacity for the government estate is therefore at procurement stage while the central bank's own is in service — the two ends of the same question, several years apart.

summary: A [17 MW dam was commissioned in June 2026](2026-06-16-regideso-inauguration-barrage-hydroelectrique-mulembwe) and [a substation now allows up to 50 MW into the capital's network](2025-08-22-burundi-eco-poste-de-rubirizi), against outages that put industry on gensets.
developments:
2025-08 — [a new transformer substation was connected to a 110 kV transmission line, allowing up to 50 MW to be injected into the capital's urban network](2025-08-22-burundi-eco-poste-de-rubirizi), reported against continuing outages that left businesses paralysed, hospitals on generators and industry on costly generating sets.

2026-06-16 — [a 17 MW hydropower dam was officially commissioned, completing a complex at 49.5 MW, built for USD 320 million](2026-06-16-regideso-inauguration-barrage-hydroelectrique-mulembwe), the largest generation addition in the window; [a nationwide 30 kV network reinforcement contract was signed the following day](2026-06-17-regideso-signature-contrat-ascent-burundi-composante-1-reseau-30kv).

The base holds no data-centre power demand figure and no water statement at all, so what is recorded is the supply side improving rather than a measured sufficiency for digital loads.

summary: The regulator [names power cuts, generator fuel and unstable supply first among six causes of degraded networks](2026-08-03-telecommunications-un-casse-tete-pour-les-abonnes), with base-station powering only [at study stage](2026-08-03-telecommunications-un-casse-tete-pour-les-abonnes).
developments:
2026-08-03 — [the regulator published its own diagnosis of degraded mobile and internet quality and named six causes: power cuts, generator fuel supply, unstable supply from the utility, urban bandwidth saturation, ageing transmission equipment and missing masts](2026-08-03-telecommunications-un-casse-tete-pour-les-abonnes). That is unchanged in kind from [the position a year earlier, when outages were attributed to power, fuel and foreign-exchange shortages](2025-09-10-unreliable-connectivity-impacts-burundi-citizens).

The response is a study. [Powering of mobile base stations is at study stage with no instrument or programme](2026-08-03-telecommunications-un-casse-tete-pour-les-abonnes), against a network the same regulator says fails mainly on electricity.

The effect reaches the systems this report tracks: the electronic invoicing machines reported under revenue collection stop whenever the power does.

summary: Access [stands at 25.9 per cent, 8 per cent on the grid and 17.9 per cent off it](2025-09-24-pacte-national-pour-energie-compact-republique-du-burundi), with [ten rural centres electrified in the year](2026-07-28-aber-assemblee-generale-personnel-bilan-2025-2026).
developments:
[The national energy compact records installed capacity of 204.882 MW and an access rate of 25.9 per cent, split 8 per cent on the interconnected grid and 17.9 per cent on decentralised solutions, against a target of 70 per cent access by 2030, a target of 300 mini-grids and USD 3.49 billion of financing need](2025-09-24-pacte-national-pour-energie-compact-republique-du-burundi).

2026-07 — [the rural electrification agency named ten rural centres electrified during its 2025-2026 year with works continuing at seven more, alongside maintenance of solar mini-grids and micro-hydro plants](2026-07-28-aber-assemblee-generale-personnel-bilan-2025-2026). Named sites rather than a connection count is what the record supports, and neither source publishes how many households were connected in the year — which is the figure a target expressed as a share of the population has to be read against.

summary: A revenue platform [entered service in August 2026](2026-08-04-obr-e-kori-plateforme-immatriculation-en-ligne) and a cross-government financial system [went out to tender](2026-03-25-pafen-aao-sigfp-systeme-integre-gestion-finances-publiques), over an estate last described in 2022.
developments:
[A project appraisal document describes the government's own estate: a government network providing about 55 public institutions with 2.5 Mbps broadband, a small network operations centre and data centre run by the state technology secretariat, fragmented ministry servers and no national data-exchange layer](2022-05-31-world-bank-burundi-digital-foundations-project-pad). No later restatement of that position is held.

2026-03 — [a request for proposals opened for the design, supply and installation of an integrated public financial management system](2026-03-25-pafen-aao-sigfp-systeme-integre-gestion-finances-publiques), the largest cross-government software replacement identified.

2026-08-04 — [the revenue authority's digitalisation platform entered service, from which date all new taxpayer registration is made exclusively online](2026-08-04-obr-e-kori-plateforme-immatriculation-en-ligne). A production system going live is a stronger statement about robustness than any procurement notice, and it is the only one the window holds.

summary: A change-management workshop [prepared administration teams to run the financial management system](2026-04-08-mfben-burundi-prepare-mise-en-place-sigfp), against [three named bodies stated to require technical assistance](2022-05-31-world-bank-burundi-digital-foundations-project-pad).
developments:
[The digital ministry, the state technology secretariat and the regulator are all stated to require technical assistance](2022-05-31-world-bank-burundi-digital-foundations-project-pad) — the base's standing position on who can run what.

2026-04-07 — [a change-management workshop began preparing public administration teams to adopt and run the integrated public financial management system](2026-04-08-mfben-burundi-prepare-mise-en-place-sigfp), aligned to the programme budget and to the national long-range vision. The distinction worth keeping is that this is appropriation of a central state system by the people who will operate it, not its procurement; no staffing establishment, certification count or retention figure is published, so the base records an intention to build capacity and not the capacity itself.

summary: Regional central bank governors [flagged financial-system cyber risk as needing stronger common measures](2026-07-27-burundi-eac-regional-payment-system-acceleration); no national instrument or common measure exists.
developments:
2026-07-27 — [East African central bank governors flagged financial-system cyber risk as requiring stronger common measures](2026-07-27-burundi-eac-regional-payment-system-acceleration). No common measure has been adopted and no baseline was held before it.

That single regional mention is the whole of the country's cybersecurity record on this ledger. No national strategy, no law, no computer emergency response team, no agency and no reported incident appears — at a point when an instant payment system, an online tax platform and a biometric identity programme have all entered service or are about to.

summary: The government's own appraisal [records fragmented ministry servers and no national data-exchange layer](2022-05-31-world-bank-burundi-digital-foundations-project-pad); the [2018 framework decree provides the basis and no platform runs on it](2018-07-25-decret-100-085-cadre-national-donnees).
developments:
[A project appraisal document records fragmented ministry servers with no national data-exchange layer](2022-05-31-world-bank-burundi-digital-foundations-project-pad) — a statement of absence in the government's own financing document rather than a gap in the record, and the position has not been restated since.

[The 2018 national data framework decree is the legal basis that would carry such a layer](2018-07-25-decret-100-085-cadre-national-donnees): it defines administrative data, brings it into the dissemination regime and provides for making data available by electronic means. No platform operates on its authority, no data-sharing agreement made under it is held, and the cross-government information-systems concept that would specify one was presented for validation in December 2024 and not adopted.

summary: Identity verification [was extended across the supervised financial sector](2026-02-13-brb-renforcement-cadre-lbc-ft) and [made compulsory for every SIM](2026-06-05-ecofin-burundi-identification-cartes-sim-obligatoire), in both cases against a document rather than a register.
developments:
2026-01-30 — [a central bank regulation and its implementing circular on customer identification, identity verification and know-your-customer extended documentary identity verification across the supervised financial sector](2026-02-13-brb-renforcement-cadre-lbc-ft). It does not make the national identity card the exclusive document and describes no query against a central register.

2026-06 — [the regulator required every subscriber to regularise SIM identification against the national identity card, with non-compliant lines deactivated from 25 June](2026-06-05-ecofin-burundi-identification-cartes-sim-obligatoire).

Both are identity being consumed as paper. [The payment-infrastructure assessment states the position underneath: national identity cards are presented as documentary evidence at account opening rather than authenticated against a register](2025-04-01-uncdf-payment-infrastructure-assessment-burundi).

summary: Common standards [were defined in April 2026 naming HL7 FHIR](2026-04-13-burundi-systeme-information-sante-interoperable-hl7-fhir), and a laboratory system [went into nine sites with automated transmission](2026-05-29-pnud-digitalisation-laboratoires-datatocare).
developments:
[The health sector digital plan records that the reporting platform, the clinical system and the logistics applications coexist without automatic transfer, that feeding between them is manual, and sets normalisation, a unique identifier, software certification and interoperability as objectives to be built](2019-01-01-pndis-ii-plan-national-informatique-sante-2020-2024).

2026-04-07 to 10 — [a national workshop defined common technical standards, notably HL7 FHIR, priority data-exchange flows and mediation for the fragmented platforms](2026-04-13-burundi-systeme-information-sante-interoperable-hl7-fhir).

2026-05-18 to 29 — [a laboratory information system was deployed to nine strategic sites, interconnecting ten diagnostic instruments to a central web platform with automated data transmission, with a national trainer pool formed to replicate across 64 instruments](2026-05-29-pnud-digitalisation-laboratoires-datatocare). That is health data actually moving between machines, which the plan of 2019 said did not happen.

summary: Ministry cadres [were trained in database administration](2026-06-07-unesco-renforcement-sige-burundi-cadres-menrs-formation-yaounde) and the system [was assessed against continental norms](2026-06-09-au-iped-supports-burundi-strengthening-education-data), from a paper-collection baseline.
developments:
[An independent assessment describes the education system's data chain as paper collection at the school followed by electronic entry at central level, published through the statistical yearbooks, with limits on integration and reliability of the databases](2023-12-19-gpe-itap-assessment-of-enabling-factors-burundi).

2026-06 — [cadres of the education ministry were trained in database administration as part of modernising the management information system](2026-06-07-unesco-renforcement-sige-burundi-cadres-menrs-formation-yaounde), and [Burundi self-assessed the system against the continental EMIS norms and standards at a three-day technical workshop](2026-06-09-au-iped-supports-burundi-strengthening-education-data), the most directly interoperability-facing education movement in the window.

What neither states is a connection to anything outside education: no link to civil registration, to the identity register or to any other sectoral system is on the record.

summary: More than a million beneficiary records [were migrated to a shared platform connected to several payment providers](2026-01-22-wb-burundi-cash-for-jobs-embracing-smart-it), with extension to the unified registry prepared.
developments:
[A technical policy note describes the position reached: the programme's management information system migrated to a shared platform, hosted in the government data centre, with modules in operation and an interfacing architecture that supports integration with identity databases — but does not confirm a live link to civil status or the national identity system](2025-07-01-implementing-core-mis-social-protection-burundi).

2026-01 — [more than a million individual beneficiary records were migrated, the system connected to several payment providers, and its extension to the unified social registry prepared](2026-01-22-wb-burundi-cash-for-jobs-embracing-smart-it).

The connection this system has made is to payments; the connection it has not made is to identity, which is the one that would let it verify who it is paying.

summary: The biometric identity card [was presented as technically ready in May 2026 and is waiting on the law or decree governing its use](2026-05-07-burundi-unveils-biometric-national-id-awaits-law), piloted in about a dozen communes.
developments:
2026-05-07 — [the card was presented as technically ready and awaiting the legal instrument governing its use, having been piloted in about a dozen communes](2026-05-07-burundi-unveils-biometric-national-id-awaits-law). The starting position was [a confirmation that it would not be ready for the 2025 voter enrolment](2024-05-24 Burundi - biometric national ID card will not be available for 2025 voter enrolment).

Whole-project cost is put at about BIF 15bn covering equipment, production centres and nationwide deployment, and [BIF 16.0bn was proposed in the following year's draft budget](2026-06-11-bdi-2026-cni-biometrique).

The order is deliberate: the government states that the data protection law came first in order to enable the card. What is still missing is the card's own instrument, an issuance figure and any statement of what it authenticates against.

summary: [83.5 per cent of under-fives were registered at the last national survey](2017-12-01-edsb-iii-enquete-demographique-sante-burundi-2016-2017); [thirteen communes now hold a biometric registration system](2026-08-11-rtnb-le-burundi-accelere-la-modernisation-de-letat-civil).
developments:
[The third demographic and health survey puts 83.5 per cent of children under five registered with the civil-status authority, 83.7 per cent of boys and 83.3 per cent of girls, reported against the sustainable development goal indicator](2017-12-01-edsb-iii-enquete-demographique-sante-burundi-2016-2017). It is the primary national statistical publication of the figure and it is now nine years old.

2026-08-10 — [the territorial administration directorate set out digitalisation of civil status in pilot communes with decentralisation to zone level, and a UN agency stated that thirteen communes already have a biometric registration system](2026-08-11-rtnb-le-burundi-accelere-la-modernisation-de-letat-civil).

What has not been published is any updated national coverage rate, so the base can date the machinery and not the population it has reached.

summary: Travel-document production [is stated to be assured entirely by ministry staff since a foreign supplier's contract expired](2023-03-09-mininter-solution-rupture-documents-voyage).
developments:
[The interior ministry records that travel-document production is assured one hundred per cent by the migration directorate's own staff since the expiry of the contract with a foreign supplier, a new supplier providing consumables only](2023-03-09-mininter-solution-rupture-documents-voyage).

It is the clearest official statement on this ledger that a credential system is nationally operated rather than vendor-run, and it is the ministry's own. What it does not carry is a volume, a backlog figure or any statement about the identity card as distinct from the passport — so the claim covers travel documents and cannot be extended to the credential estate as a whole.

summary: A border system [reads and verifies passports at the international airport against international police databases](2025-08-17-maeircd-magazine-no7-border-management-system), the first authentication on the ledger.
developments:
2025-08 — [a border management system was launched at the international airport, automating reading and verification of passports with a direct interconnection to international police databases, announced for progressive extension to other border posts](2025-08-17-maeircd-magazine-no7-border-management-system). It is the first instance on this ledger of a credential being checked against anything rather than simply read.

What it authenticates against is a foreign database, not a Burundian one. [The domestic position is that national identity is presented as documentary evidence rather than authenticated against a register](2025-04-01-uncdf-payment-infrastructure-assessment-burundi), and no extension of the border system beyond the airport is recorded.

summary: The civil registry's link to health facilities [now runs in 123 facilities and has recorded more than 52,000 births](2026-08-11-burundi-civil-registry-digitization-biometric-id), on the interior ministry's own count.
developments:
2026-08-11 — [the civil-registry to health-facility link for birth registration, piloted since 2023 and institutionalised in 2024, is stated to run in 123 health facilities and to have recorded more than 52,000 births](2026-08-11-burundi-civil-registry-digitization-biometric-id). The figures are the ministry's own and no coverage denominator is given, so the share of births captured is not knowable from the record.

[A national unique identifier is planned with fingerprint and facial biometrics](2026-08-13-burundi-decentralization-civil-registry-digitization-abp), which would be the link from registration at birth to a credential. Nothing states when, or how a child registered through a health facility today obtains one.

summary: The country's own account [states civil registration is not yet interoperable with the future digital identity](2026-07-18-burundi-crvs-transformation-journey); [interoperability with health facilities is planned](2026-08-11-rtnb-le-burundi-accelere-la-modernisation-de-letat-civil).
developments:
2026-07 — [Burundi's country presentation to the African registrars general meeting states the position plainly: paper-based and manual elements persist, there is no single national civil-status database, and civil registration is not yet fully interoperable with the future national digital identification system](2026-07-18-burundi-crvs-transformation-journey).

2026-08-10 — [the territorial administration directorate set out planned interoperability with health facilities for births and deaths, with notification through hill chiefs, alongside a national digital identity carrying a unique identifier and biometrics](2026-08-11-rtnb-le-burundi-accelere-la-modernisation-de-letat-civil).

The two accounts a month apart give the shape of it: the link is designed and not built, and the register it would connect to does not yet exist as a single database.

summary: There is [no central national identity database able to support digital know-your-customer](2025-04-01-uncdf-payment-infrastructure-assessment-burundi); identity is consumed as a document, not as a query.
developments:
[A payment-infrastructure assessment records that the national identity system is non-biometric and that there is no central national identity database able to support digital know-your-customer, national identity cards being presented as documentary evidence at account opening rather than authenticated against a register](2025-04-01-uncdf-payment-infrastructure-assessment-burundi). It distinguishes identity interoperability from the payment switch, which does exist.

That is the position the whole of this chapter rests on. Every system that requires identity in the window — the financial sector's customer identification rules, compulsory SIM registration, social protection enrolment — verifies a piece of paper, because there is nothing to ask.

summary: The central bank [migrated the payment switch to the international messaging standard](2026-02-05-burundi-upgrades-payment-system-iso-20022) and [issued five anti-money-laundering circulars](2026-02-16-burundi-central-bank-new-aml-cft-rules).
developments:
2026-02-05 — [the payment switch was migrated to the ISO 20022 messaging standard](2026-02-05-burundi-upgrades-payment-system-iso-20022), from a position of not being migrated. It is the technical precondition for the instant payment system launched two months later and for the regional accessions reported under cross-border functionality.

2026-02-16 — [five central bank circulars on anti-money-laundering and counter-terrorist financing were issued, aligned to the international standard-setter's recommendations](2026-02-16-burundi-central-bank-new-aml-cft-rules), where no baseline was held.

Both are the bank acting as scheme owner rather than as supervisor: no oversight report, scheme rulebook or published sanction appears on this ledger, and the mandatory-integration penalty reported below is the only enforcement instrument on record.

summary: Social transfers [reach recipients over their own mobile phones](2025-09-22-sos-medias-burundi-fin-merankabandi-transferts-monetaires-refugies), and the beneficiary system is now [connected to several payment providers](2026-01-22-wb-burundi-cash-for-jobs-embracing-smart-it).
developments:
2025-09 — [a cash-transfer programme closed in one province after two years, having paid 73,600 BIF every two months over recipients' own mobile phones, 72,000 BIF net of the withdrawal charge](2025-09-22-sos-medias-burundi-fin-merankabandi-transferts-monetaires-refugies). It is the clearest record the base holds of a government-to-person digital channel reaching a specific population, and the withdrawal charge is the part worth keeping: the recipient pays to take the money out.

2026-01 — [the successor system migrated more than a million individual beneficiary records and was connected to several payment providers](2026-01-22-wb-burundi-cash-for-jobs-embracing-smart-it), which is the structural change: payment routed through a system rather than through one programme's arrangement.

progress: Advanced, with the invoicing machines stopping whenever the power does
summary: The online tax platform [took over all new taxpayer registration from 4 August 2026](2026-08-06-burundi-e-kori-online-taxpayer-registration-mandatory), while [invoicing machines stop with every power cut](2026-08-20-abp-karusi-electronic-billing-power-cuts).
developments:
2026-01-19 — [the online tax platform launched for declaration and payment](2026-01-20-burundi-revenue-authority-e-kori-digital-tax-platform), [reported at the time as the country's first](2026-01-22 Burundi launches online tax system e-KORI). 2026-08-04 — [all new taxpayer registration became exclusively online through it, for natural and legal persons and cooperatives, with commercial registration routed through the business agency's portal, cooperative registration through the cooperatives agency, and biometric enrolment for natural persons](2026-08-06-burundi-e-kori-online-taxpayer-registration-mandatory).

2025-12-25 — [the revised finance law requires banks to transfer telepaid taxes daily, with a penalty of 100% of the amount collected for missing the deadline](2025-12-25-burundi-mfben-loi-finances-2025-2026-revisee-defense-parlement).

Against it, 2026-08-20 — [traders in one province report that electronic invoicing machines stop working whenever the power does, halting sales and invoice issuance with every outage, with operators of weak literacy or digital skills reported to struggle](2026-08-20-abp-karusi-electronic-billing-power-cuts). Delivery had stood at [500 of 10,000 machines ordered](2024-12-24-iwacu-revision-budgetaire-2024-2025-imprevus). No national outage figure, downtime measure or offline-mode provision is published.

summary: A national instant payment system [launched in April 2026 with interoperability across banks, microfinance and payment institutions](2026-04-23-brb-lancement-burundipay).
developments:
2025-09-18 — [managers of public funds were required to obtain an electronic-billing-machine invoice from suppliers before payment, on pain of a 20 per cent penalty](2025-09-18-obr-facture-machine-electronique-exigence-gestionnaires-fonds-publics) — a digital control placed inside the government-to-supplier payment cycle.

2026-04-23 — [the national instant payment system was launched, built under the World Bank-supported foundations project and providing full interoperability between commercial banks, microfinance institutions and payment institutions](2026-04-23-brb-lancement-burundipay).

[The central bank reports annually on the clearing house, the real-time gross settlement system, the national switch and electronic money](2025-11-01-brb-rapport-annuel-systemes-moyens-paiement-surveillance-2024), so a series exists; no transaction volume or value for the new instant system is yet published.

summary: The national instant payment system [launched in April 2026 and had 17 of 78 licensed institutions live by August](2026-08-06-burundi-burundipay-instant-payment-uptake-brb), with the four mobile-money systems interoperable.
developments:
2026-04-23 — [the national instant payment platform launched publicly, connecting banks, microfinance institutions and mobile money on the international messaging standard and USSD at around 1,000 transactions per second](2026-04-25-burundipay-platform-connects-banks-microfinance-mobile-money), [reported as Africa's twenty-second live instant payment system](2026-04-28-burundipay-real-time-payments-platform-wearetech).

2026-08-06 — [17 of 78 licensed institutions were in production by 4 August 2026 — five commercial banks, ten microfinance institutions and two payment institutions — with about 224,000 users and cumulative transaction volume of about BIF 4.29bn, and integration mandatory for all licensed institutions by 5 September 2026 under a penalty of BIF 1m per month of delay](2026-08-06-burundi-burundipay-instant-payment-uptake-brb).

2026-06-12 — [the four mobile-money systems are named as interoperable through it](2026-06-12-burundi-eco-digitalisation-services-publics), where they had not been. Fewer than a quarter of licensed institutions are live four months after launch, which is what the September deadline and its penalty exist to change.

summary: Cash [held about 45% of digital-payment value, with about 1.6m of 7.6m mobile wallets active](2025-09-29-burundi-digital-payments-growth-cash-dominates) in the last reading the base holds.
developments:
2025-09-29 — central bank data for the second quarter of 2025 [put deposits and withdrawals at about 45% of digital-payment value and about 1.6m of 7.6m mobile wallets active](2025-09-29-burundi-digital-payments-growth-cash-dominates). No baseline preceded it and no reading has followed it.

The dormancy rate is the finding: roughly four in five wallets opened are not in use, which bounds what the instant payment system reported above can reach. [Its own user figure of about 224,000](2026-08-06-burundi-burundipay-instant-payment-uptake-brb) sits against those registered wallets.

No quarterly series, no account-ownership survey and no financial-inclusion strategy appears anywhere on this ledger.

summary: The central bank [acceded to the pan-African settlement system with four banks authorised](2026-08-06-burundi-burundipay-instant-payment-uptake-brb) and [expects to join the East African payment system by December 2026](2026-08-19-theeastafrican-burundi-eaps-december-2026).
developments:
2026-08-06 — [the central bank has acceded to the Pan-African Payment and Settlement System, with four Burundian banks authorised to participate as at 4 August 2026](2026-08-06-burundi-burundipay-instant-payment-uptake-brb). The accession date itself is not stated, only that it has occurred, and [the continental trade secretariat discussed the system as an implementation instrument during its August mission](2026-08-06-afcfta-secretary-general-begins-official-mission-to-burundi).

2026-08-19 — [the bank told the region's monetary affairs committee it expects to be inside the East African Payment System by December 2026, having migrated its settlement infrastructure to the international messaging standard](2026-08-19-theeastafrican-burundi-eaps-december-2026), and [has begun connecting domestic banks, the post office and the central bank to the COMESA regional payment and settlement system through technical training](2026-08-19-channelafrica-burundi-comesa-payment-integration). [Regional acceleration of the payment system was pressed at the July governors' meeting](2026-07-27-burundi-eac-regional-payment-system-acceleration).

Two accessions and one expectation, with no go-live date, participant list or transaction volume published for any of them.

progress: Advanced, an injunction with no sanction and no reported improvement
summary: The regulator [ordered an operator to make value-added-service subscription genuinely voluntary](2026-07-24-iwacu-consentement-explicite-abonne-services-valeur-ajoutee), and the consumer association reports no significant improvement two months on.
developments:
2026-07-24 — [injunctions were issued requiring genuinely voluntary subscription to value-added services and prior notification of subscribers](2026-07-24-iwacu-consentement-explicite-abonne-services-valeur-ajoutee), where no such instrument existed. The consumer association reports no significant improvement two months on, no sanction is on file, and the operator maintains that nothing activates without a customer's deliberate action.

It is the only enforcement action of any kind on this ledger, and it came from the telecommunications regulator rather than from the data protection authority the January 2026 law creates, which is not on record as operating. Nothing states how many subscribers were charged, or whether any money was refunded.

progress: No change, the instituting texts remain unadopted
summary: The national identification file [has an administrative procedure page and no instituting instrument](2026-01-01-isoko-fichier-national-identification-carte-nationale-identite); further texts remain to be adopted.
developments:
[The official administrative procedure page for the Fichier National d'Identification and the national identity card states that further texts remain to be adopted to institute the file](2026-01-01-isoko-fichier-national-identification-carte-nationale-identite).

A population register that issues a card without an instrument constituting it is the position this row records, and it is the reason every identity question in this report resolves to a document rather than to a database. The page itself carries no date and served an expired security certificate when it was captured, which is a small fact about how much of this estate is maintained.

summary: Biometric enrolment [is operating in 13 pilot communes and decentralised to zone level](2026-08-13-burundi-decentralization-civil-registry-digitization-abp), with [84% of under-fives registered but 66% holding a certificate](2026-08-11-burundi-civil-registry-digitization-biometric-id).
developments:
2026-08-13 — [biometric enrolment for the digital civil registry is operating in 13 pilot communes and has been decentralised to zone level](2026-08-13-burundi-decentralization-civil-registry-digitization-abp), against a starting position in which [the platform had been presented, every citizen was to re-register afresh and a family-code amendment was required](2026-05-08-burundi-digital-civil-registry-biometric-id-wearetech).

2026-08-11 — coverage was stated on Africa Civil Registration Day: [84% of under-fives registered at birth and 66% holding a birth certificate](2026-08-11-burundi-civil-registry-digitization-biometric-id), on a survey whose date is not given. The eighteen-point gap between registration and certificate is the finding, and it is the gap a digital registry is supposed to close.

[The ambitions and constraints of the programme were set out in May](2026-05-08-burundi-eco-carte-identite-biometrique-ambitions-defis). No national rollout timetable beyond the pilot communes is published.

summary: An urban property-owner census [began building a geo-referenced register with a unique identifier per parcel](2026-07-16-abp-lancement-recensement-proprietaires-centres-urbains-rppcub-2026), over [postal address formats](2025-11-01-upu-burundi-addressing-country-file).
developments:
[An international addressing country file gives the national postal address formats](2025-11-01-upu-burundi-addressing-country-file) — the whole of what the base held on addressing.

2026-07-14 — [an urban property-owner census was launched to build a digitised, geo-referenced land register with a unique identifier per parcel, interoperable with other national registers and feeding a web mapping service and future digital land titles](2026-07-16-abp-lancement-recensement-proprietaires-centres-urbains-rppcub-2026), first phase covering three communes of the capital and three towns, at about 3 billion BIF, with enumeration in August and September 2026.

It is an address register arriving as a property register, which is a different object: it will number parcels and their owners rather than places, and no plan to extend it beyond the six urban areas is stated.

summary: The commercial register [is established in the 2015 code](2015-01-16-burundi-loi-1-01-code-de-commerce-registre-commerce-societes), and the historic manual stock [is being converted onto a digital platform](2026-06-01-adb-prolongation-delais-reenregistrement-plateforme-digitale-immatriculation).
developments:
