[Title V of the commercial code establishes the registre de commerce et des societes and the tax identification register and names the holding agency](2015-01-16-burundi-loi-1-01-code-de-commerce-registre-commerce-societes) — the statutory basis, in force since 2015.

2026-06 — [the development agency extended the window for persons and companies recorded under the old manual register to re-register free of charge on the digital platform](2026-06-01-adb-prolongation-delais-reenregistrement-plateforme-digitale-immatriculation). That operation is what converts a historic paper stock into a digital register, and an extension is what happens when it is going slowly; no count of firms re-registered, no total on the old register and no closing date for the manual one is published.

summary: The unified social registry holds [249,671 households against a target of 290,000](2026-06-30-le-renouveau-projet-merankabandi-ii-bilan-mi-parcours), across all 3,044 collines and quartiers.
developments:
[The unified social registry and its management system are the foundation of the national social protection system, reused by two named programmes](2026-05-01-worldbank-building-burundi-national-social-protection-systems).

2026-06-16 — [the national social protection commission put the state of the registry on its own oversight agenda at its ninth annual general assembly](2026-06-16-abp-lancement-9eme-assemblee-generale-cnps), alongside the programme and the 2024-2033 national policy.

2026-06-30 — [the modernised system is deployed in the government data centre and 249,671 households are recorded against a final target of 290,000, with coverage extending to all 3,044 collines and quartiers](2026-06-30-le-renouveau-projet-merankabandi-ii-bilan-mi-parcours). It is the most completely reported register on this ledger: a count, a denominator, a target and a host.

summary: Preparations for the 2027 electoral register [are under way and contested, with opposition parties demanding suspension](2026-05-09-burundi-opposition-challenge-ceni-2027-election-preparations); no biometric card is in use.
developments:
2026-05-09 — [opposition parties demanded suspension of the electoral commission's preparations for the 2027 register](2026-05-09-burundi-opposition-challenge-ceni-2027-election-preparations). No baseline was held before it and the substance of the objection is not resolved on the record.

The biometric card that might have underpinned the roll is not in use: it [was confirmed as unavailable for the 2025 enrolment](2024-05-24 Burundi - biometric national ID card will not be available for 2025 voter enrolment) and [is still waiting on its governing instrument](2026-05-07-burundi-unveils-biometric-national-id-awaits-law).

So the register is being prepared on the old basis, under objection, while the credential intended to modernise it sits ready and unusable. No enrolment figure, audit or de-duplication statement is published.

summary: Registration [exists but is not integrated with filing and payment](2026-06-03-imf-burundi-selected-issues-cr-26-151), and the [value-added tax threshold was reset from 1 July 2026](2026-07-01-obr-communique-contribuables-chiffre-affaires-25-millions-tva).
developments:
[An international assessment records the register's position: taxpayer registration exists but is not yet integrated with the filing and payment modules, the revenue platform is phased to full operation around mid-2027, and about 13,000 electronic billing machines are deployed against a 40,000 target](2026-06-03-imf-burundi-selected-issues-cr-26-151).

2026-07-01 — [the value-added tax threshold was set at 25,000,000 BIF of taxable turnover under a statute of 30 June 2026, with invoicing from 1 July and monthly declaration by the fifteenth](2026-07-01-obr-communique-contribuables-chiffre-affaires-25-millions-tva). A threshold change is a change in who the register must carry, which is the register question rather than the platform question, and no count of taxpayers on either side of it is published.

progress: Advanced, with the mandatory fee contested
summary: Land titles [are digitised, with about 123,000 holders to be secured](2026-06-12-burundi-eco-digitalisation-services-publics), and [a mandatory electronic-title fee drew objections on cost and deadline](2026-04-01-titres-fonciers-securises-mesure-couteuse-precipitee).
developments:
[Land services were digitised on an integrated platform in June 2025](2025-06-18 Burundi's Land Services Go Digital with New Integrated Platform), and 2026-06-12 — [the minister's stock-take put about 123,000 title holders as those to be secured digitally](2026-06-12-burundi-eco-digitalisation-services-publics).

2026-04-01 — [an ordinance making the electronic land title fee mandatory drew objections on its cost and on the shortness of its deadline](2026-04-01-titres-fonciers-securises-mesure-couteuse-precipitee). No response, revision or enforcement figure has followed.

It is the most complete register on this ledger and the only one charging the public directly to use it. No count of titles actually converted, no processing time and no dispute figure is published.

summary: The health supply-chain system [reached all public and faith-based facilities, 956 in total with more than 2,000 users](2026-06-26-burundi-elmis-medexis-health-rollout-wearetech), from a partial rollout.
developments:
2026-06-26 — [the electronic logistics management and medicine-exchange system reached all public and faith-based facilities: 956 facilities and more than 2,000 users](2026-06-26-burundi-elmis-medexis-health-rollout-wearetech), against a partial rollout at the start of the window.

It is the most completely deployed sectoral system on this ledger by facility coverage. What is not published is what it produces: no stock-out rate, no order cycle time and no data-quality measure appears, so the record shows a system installed everywhere and nothing about whether the supply chain it manages improved.

The other health system on the ledger is the civil-registry link running in 123 facilities, reported under digital identity from birth.

summary: A monitoring tool for technical and vocational training centres [was validated on 7 August 2026](2026-08-07-burundi-cem-cfp-digital-monitoring-tool-eu-funded), with no deployment date or centre count stated.
developments:
2026-08-07 — [a digital tool for tracking the institutional performance of technical and vocational training centres in real time was validated, built by a youth organisation under a European Union-backed project](2026-08-07-burundi-cem-cfp-digital-monitoring-tool-eu-funded). Nothing of the kind was held before it.

No deployment date, centre count or custodian ministry is stated, so what exists is a validated tool without an owner. It is the only education system on this ledger: no school census platform, enrolment system, teacher registry or examination system appears for the country.

summary: The social transfer programme [completed migration to an open-source insurance platform, covering 1.25m beneficiaries](2026-01-01 Burundi's growing social protection system now runs on openIMIS).
developments:
[Migration of the national social transfer programme onto the open-source insurance management platform completed, covering 1.25m beneficiaries](2026-01-01 Burundi's growing social protection system now runs on openIMIS), from a position of migration under way.

That is the largest beneficiary base of any government system on this ledger. Nothing is published about how payments reach those beneficiaries, whether the platform connects to the civil registry being digitised in parallel, or what identity is used to enrol — three questions the instant payment system and the biometric card reported elsewhere would each bear on.

summary: An offline case-digitisation platform [was deployed with thirteen scanning kits across the courts](2026-06-11-bsf-appel-offres-evaluation-fin-projet-composante-numerisation-pasju) and is now at end-of-project evaluation.
developments:
[Technical assistance to the justice sector covered archiving, computerisation of court registries and case management, with a judicial-statistics collection system, servers and training behind it](2024-03-26-coginta-technical-assistance-justice-sector-support-programme-burundi-at-pasju).

2026-06-11 — [terms of reference for the end-of-project evaluation give the clearest published account of what was actually deployed: an offline platform for digitising and classifying pending case files, with thirteen scanning kits, across the supreme court, the appeal courts, the high courts and the prosecution offices of the targeted provinces](2026-06-11-bsf-appel-offres-evaluation-fin-projet-composante-numerisation-pasju).

Offline is the operative word. A case-management estate that does not connect its courts is a filing improvement rather than a system, and the evaluation being tendered is the point at which someone finds out which it became.

summary: The revenue platform [went into production on 4 August 2026 as the exclusive registration channel](2026-08-04-obr-e-kori-plateforme-immatriculation-en-ligne), and billing-machine enforcement [moved from distribution to inspection](2026-04-16-abp-machines-facturation-sous-controle-fraude-fiscale).
developments:
2026-01-19 — [the integrated digitalisation of internal-revenue management was officially launched](2026-01-20-burundi-lancement-projet-e-kori-gestion-integree-recettes-internes).

2026-04-08 — [the revenue office moved from distributing electronic billing machines to checking their use: over 13,000 machines distributed nationally, capital inspections finding machines unused and non-conforming invoices, and buyers without an invoice liable to a 20 per cent penalty](2026-04-16-abp-machines-facturation-sous-controle-fraude-fiscale).

2026-08-04 — [the platform entered service, from which date all new taxpayer registration applications are made exclusively online, with three routes for natural persons, legal persons and cooperatives and a biometric appointment step](2026-08-04-obr-e-kori-plateforme-immatriculation-en-ligne). A system that becomes the only channel is the strongest form of adoption and the one with the most exposure: no uptime figure, throughput or fallback is stated.

summary: The revenue authority's electronic single window [entered production with a pharmaceutical-import module](2026-02-19-burundi-guichet-unique-importation-wearetech).
developments:
2026-02-19 — [the electronic single window was put into production](2026-02-19-burundi-guichet-unique-importation-wearetech), [carrying a module for pharmaceutical imports run with the medicines regulator](2026-02-19-burundi-abrema-pharmaceutical-imports-techafricanews). None existed before it.

One module in production is the whole of the record. No clearance volume, processing time or trader count is published, and no other agency is stated to have joined. The window sits alongside the online tax platform reported under revenue collection, and nothing states whether the two exchange anything.

summary: A joint ministerial ordinance [set the terms on which the secured electronic land title is acquired](2026-02-09-burundi-ordonnance-550-540-998-titre-foncier-electronique-securise), under the amended finance law.
developments:
2026-02-06 — [a joint ministerial ordinance set the terms on which the secured electronic land title is acquired, under article 142 of the amended finance law](2026-02-09-burundi-ordonnance-550-540-998-titre-foncier-electronique-securise). It is the point at which digitisation of the land title moves from budget intent to an instrument that applies to a transaction.

What is held is the ministry's announcement rather than the operative text, so the fee, the procedure and the register the title is issued against cannot be read. No count of titles issued electronically, and no connection to the urban property census building a parcel identifier, is on the record.

progress: Advanced, on announcements rather than on a countable service estate
summary: One-stop service desks [are under operationalisation with archive management still largely manual](2026-07-31-burundi-public-administration-reforms-digitisation-citizen-services), a [paperless Council of Ministers is reported](2026-06-12-burundi-eco-digitalisation-services-publics), and [a finance system award is contested](2026-04-20-digital-business-africa-burundi-sigfp-bi-gre-a-gre).
developments:
2026-07-31 — [operationalisation of one-stop service desks is named in the civil-service ministry's reform programme, with the ministry itself stating that archive management is still largely manual and service digitisation unfinished](2026-07-31-burundi-public-administration-reforms-digitisation-citizen-services).

2026-06-12 — [a paperless Council of Ministers is reported as operating](2026-06-12-burundi-eco-digitalisation-services-publics), with no instrument or date published.

2026-04-20 — [the integrated public finance management system is under procurement at an envelope of about US$30m, and the single-source award is contested by a non-governmental organisation](2026-04-20-digital-business-africa-burundi-sigfp-bi-gre-a-gre). The allegations are reported and not established, and no primary from the organisation or the ministry is held.

No count of services available online, no service catalogue and no usage figure appears anywhere for the country.

summary: A [USD 10 million contract was signed to extend rural 4G](2026-03-03-setic-pafen-lumitel-connectivite-4g-milieu-rural) and [equipment was handed to governors and communal administrators](2026-08-14-le-renouveau-pnud-don-gouverneurs-administrateurs-communaux), from a base of non-functioning networks.
developments:
[A country diagnostic records broadband deployment to commune level as achieved while the multiservice telecentre per commune and the intranet and e-government services were not, and describes the government network as not functioning effectively in most government units](2020-01-01-burundi-digital-economy-assessment).

2026-03 — [a USD 10 million contract was signed to extend 4G broadband in rural areas, co-financed 44 per cent by government and 56 per cent by the operator, tied to access to digital public services](2026-03-03-setic-pafen-lumitel-connectivite-4g-milieu-rural).

2026-08 — [a development agency handed laptops, uninterruptible power supplies, printers and photocopiers to provincial governors and communal administrators](2026-08-14-le-renouveau-pnud-don-gouverneurs-administrateurs-communaux), the most direct addition to equipment held by local government offices in the window. No count of communes reached by either is published.

summary: A ministry platform [is being built to collect data from the communes to central level](2026-03-16-mininter-vers-une-solution-numerique-innovante-production-gestion-donnees), alongside [a geo-referenced urban parcel register](2026-07-16-abp-lancement-recensement-proprietaires-centres-urbains-rppcub-2026).
developments:
[A technical manual governs the communal land services and zonal land counters, covering institutional anchoring, premises, IT equipment, staffing and the handling of certificates and registers, including tablet-based collection and electronic production and archiving](2024-11-01-manuel-technique-gestion-fonctionnement-services-fonciers-communaux-burundi) — the most technically explicit instrument the base holds for a record kept at commune level.

2026-03-12 — [a workshop presented a platform under development to collect data from the communes up to central level across territorial administration, civil status, migration, public security, cooperatives and disaster management, with a pilot scheduled for May 2026 and over a thousand users to be trained](2026-03-16-mininter-vers-une-solution-numerique-innovante-production-gestion-donnees); participants named internet availability and infrastructure as the constraints.

2026-07-14 — [an urban property-owner census began building a digitised, geo-referenced register with a unique identifier per parcel](2026-07-16-abp-lancement-recensement-proprietaires-centres-urbains-rppcub-2026).

summary: A laboratory system [went into nine sites with automated transmission](2026-05-29-pnud-digitalisation-laboratoires-datatocare), and a mass campaign [ran on digital household registration and barcode scanning](2026-02-01-pnlp-campagne-distribution-mii-digitalisee-2025-experience-burundi).
developments:
2026-05-18 to 29 — [a laboratory information system was deployed to nine strategic sites, interconnecting ten diagnostic instruments to a central web platform with automated data transmission, with a national trainer pool formed to replicate across 64 instruments](2026-05-29-pnud-digitalisation-laboratoires-datatocare).

[The 2025 insecticide-treated-net mass campaign was run on digital household registration and stock management with barcode and QR scanning and real-time tracking](2026-02-01-pnlp-campagne-distribution-mii-digitalisee-2025-experience-burundi), the account carrying the challenges met and the lessons drawn as well as the design.

Both are digital capture reaching where patients are rather than reporting from where they were seen. Neither states how many of the sites are rural, which is the question this indicator asks and the record does not answer.

summary: Tenders opened for [digital centres at ten rural and peri-urban learning centres](2026-06-09-le-renouveau-peappjf-avis-appel-offres-equipements-informatiques-centres-numeriques) and [585 computers across 39 central schools](2026-08-11-unicef-rfp-equipements-informatiques-39-ecoles-centrales).
developments:
[An independent assessment describes school data as paper collection at the school followed by electronic entry at central level, with no demonstrated direct electronic capture at rural fondamental schools](2023-12-19-gpe-itap-assessment-of-enabling-factors-burundi).

2026-06 — [a tender opened for IT equipment and the operationalisation of a multimedia centre, digital centres and distance-learning platforms for a polytechnic training centre and ten rural and peri-urban learning centres, and for computers and tablets for data collection](2026-06-09-le-renouveau-peappjf-avis-appel-offres-equipements-informatiques-centres-numeriques).

2026-08-11 — [a national request for proposals opened for computer equipment in 39 central schools in three former provinces, its bill of quantities naming 585 computers and uninterruptible power supplies](2026-08-11-unicef-rfp-equipements-informatiques-39-ecoles-centrales). Both are procurement rather than delivery: no installed count, no connectivity provision and no maintenance arrangement is stated for either.

summary: A digital civil-registration platform [is piloted in a first group of communes](2026-05-06-le-renouveau-plateforme-digitale-etat-civil-cni-biometrique), with [thirteen communes stated to hold a biometric system](2026-08-11-rtnb-le-burundi-accelere-la-modernisation-de-letat-civil).
developments:
2026-05-06 — [the interior ministry presented a digital civil-registration platform and biometric national identity card production, piloted in a first group of communes with intended extension to zone level](2026-05-06-le-renouveau-plateforme-digitale-etat-civil-cni-biometrique).

2026-08-10 — [the same directorate set out digitalisation in pilot communes and decentralisation to zone level, with planned interoperability with health facilities for births and deaths notified through hill chiefs, and a UN agency stated that thirteen communes already have a biometric registration system](2026-08-11-rtnb-le-burundi-accelere-la-modernisation-de-letat-civil).

Thirteen communes is the only number on the record. Burundi has well over a hundred, so what is established is a pilot that has been running for at least a quarter and a national position that has not moved.

progress: No change, a platform reported under build with no pilot launched
summary: A centralised geolocated police platform [is reported under build with the pilot not yet launched](2025-12-04-digital-business-africa-transition-numerique-burundi-securite-routiere); no provincial post is named.
developments:
[A centralised, geolocated data platform is reported under build for the national and judicial police: real-time checking of licences, insurance and roadworthiness, a geographic information system for patrol tracking and intervention analysis, and interconnection between police, transport, insurers, revenue and telecoms, with a pilot still to be launched](2025-12-04-digital-business-africa-transition-numerique-burundi-securite-routiere).

It is the only entry the base holds on police data capture. The source names no commissariat or police post in the provinces, so whether any of this reaches a rural station is not established — which is the whole of what this indicator asks.

summary: No artificial-intelligence system was identified in operational use in Burundian public administration; [data is described as under-used and often unfit for advanced analytics](2026-07-01-undp-reading-ai-readiness-backwards-country-insights).
developments:
[A synthesis of country readiness assessments carries the analysis for Burundi: institutions produce more data but it remains largely under-used and often unfit for advanced analytics, and strengthening those foundations is set out as a precondition for reliable adoption](2026-07-01-undp-reading-ai-readiness-backwards-country-insights).

The finding is an evidenced absence rather than a gap in the record, and it is the more useful of the two. It also explains the shape of the rest of this chapter: the one artificial-intelligence deployment the base holds sits inside a health workflow run with an external partner, not inside an administration.

summary: A malaria diagnostic tool [entered pilot in two provinces](2024-10-15-enabel-amelioration-diagnostic-paludisme-burundi-outil-pilote-ia), and work is under way on [a national malaria data warehouse](2026-03-31-bluesquare-structurer-utilisation-donnees-lutte-paludisme-burundi).
developments:
2024-10 — [a development agency, the health ministry and the malaria programme introduced an artificial-intelligence reading of malaria rapid diagnostic tests, with a demonstration workshop and a pilot in two provinces](2024-10-15-enabel-amelioration-diagnostic-paludisme-burundi-outil-pilote-ia). It is the one evidenced case of artificial intelligence in operational use inside a Burundian sector workflow.

2026-03 — [work with the health ministry, the malaria programme, the health information directorate and the sector's IT directorate is building a national malaria data warehouse, with the diagnostic tool described as still at pilot stage](2026-03-31-bluesquare-structurer-utilisation-donnees-lutte-paludisme-burundi).

Two years on, still a pilot. The warehouse is the more consequential half: a sectoral data layer is what a model would have to run on, and it is the thing the readiness assessment says is missing.

summary: Two local artificial-intelligence builds [were named at a July 2026 workshop](2026-07-27-burundi-abadaad-ai-governance-data-ethics-workshop), with no funding, user base or public deployment on file.
developments:
2026-07-27 — [two local builds were named at a governance and data ethics workshop](2026-07-27-burundi-abadaad-ai-governance-data-ethics-workshop), where nothing had been held before. No funding, user base or public deployment is recorded for either.

They are the whole of the country's artificial-intelligence production on this ledger, against a strategy validated three months earlier that names innovation and incubators as one of its six pillars and about fifteen health and agriculture pilots. None of those pilots has been reported as starting, and no national computing capacity exists for any of them to run on.

summary: The only governance activity on record is [one workshop, run by an alumni association rather than a regulator](2026-07-27-burundi-abadaad-ai-governance-data-ethics-workshop), whose finding was that the country holds information rather than usable data.
developments:
2026-07-27 — [the first documented workshop on artificial-intelligence governance and data ethics was run by an alumni association rather than by a regulator, and found that the country holds information rather than structured, consented, usable data](2026-07-27-burundi-abadaad-ai-governance-data-ethics-workshop).

No supervisory authority, code of practice, procurement rule or incident is on record. The national strategy names governance and ethics as its first pillar and no instrument has followed it, so the position is unchanged: the ethics of automated decision-making are being discussed by volunteers, and the data protection authority that would have jurisdiction has not been constituted.

summary: A Burundian company [is reported to have built and deployed a crop-disease diagnosis tool covering 37 diseases across seven crops](2026-02-27-global-south-world-ai-app-burundian-farmers-crop-diseases).
developments:
[A Burundian company is reported to have built and deployed a machine-learning crop-disease diagnosis and prediction tool covering 37 diseases across seven crops](2026-02-27-global-south-world-ai-app-burundian-farmers-crop-diseases).

It is taken as evidence of national capacity in digital-technology production — a domestically built software product — rather than as evidence of artificial intelligence inside a government system, which is recorded separately and is absent. The account is a single trade report whose own two date lines disagree; no user count, revenue figure, accuracy measure or independent evaluation is held, so what the base can state is that the capacity exists and not how widely it is used.

summary: A hub [reports incubating a programme targeting 40,000 entrepreneurs across two cities](2026-02-11-bujahub-moonshot-program), and [government published an account of a national digital festival](2026-06-30-setic-ouverture-solennelle-festival-numerique-junetech-2026).
developments:
[A field-based mapping of the entrepreneurship and innovation sector lists hubs and support organisations with a gap analysis, and is explicitly not an exhaustive register](2024-01-23-orange-corners-ecosystem-mapping-burundi) — so no national hub count can be taken from it, and none exists elsewhere in the base.

2026-02 — [a hub set out its own incubation role in a national programme run with government, a development agency and three financing bodies, targeting 40,000 young and women entrepreneurs, with facilities in two cities](2026-02-11-bujahub-moonshot-program). Self-published, so the reach is the hub's own claim.

2026-06-24 — [a national digital festival was opened by the finance and digital economy ministry, organised with a professional centre and the World Bank project](2026-06-30-setic-ouverture-solennelle-festival-numerique-junetech-2026) — a government account of a hub-run event, which is the firmer of the two records.

summary: A business-plan competition [opened to small enterprises with the digital economy among its priority sectors](2026-03-19-prete-nyunganira-lancement-concours-plans-affaires-copa), from a base of [no venture or angel finance](2020-01-01-burundi-digital-economy-assessment).
developments:
[A country diagnostic states digital entrepreneurship is embryonic, with one tech hub and no venture capital or angel finance](2020-01-01-burundi-digital-economy-assessment).

2026-03-16 — [a World Bank-financed project launched a business-plan competition supporting micro, small and medium enterprises, with information technology and the digital economy among the priority sectors](2026-03-19-prete-nyunganira-lancement-concours-plans-affaires-copa). It is the largest in-window support and finance mechanism reaching Burundian startups and it is not startup-specific, which is itself the finding: the country has no startup act, no dedicated fund and no incubator financing line on this ledger.

No award, cohort size or committed amount has been published against the competition.

summary: A change-management workshop [prepared administration teams to run the financial management system](2026-04-08-mfben-burundi-prepare-mise-en-place-sigfp), against a component with [no target or certification stated](2023-04-24-pafen-facilitateurs-services-publics-numeriques).
developments:
[The shared-infrastructure component of the national foundations project states that all its activities include targeted awareness initiatives and digital-skills training, principally for government officials who use, manage and maintain the shared infrastructure](2023-04-24-pafen-facilitateurs-services-publics-numeriques). No target number, obligation or certification is stated.

2026-04-07 — [a change-management workshop began preparing public administration teams to adopt and run the integrated public financial management system](2026-04-08-mfben-burundi-prepare-mise-en-place-sigfp), which is the first named cohort the base holds rather than a component description.

Still no establishment figure, completion count or certification standard, so the base can record that training happens and not how many officials can use the systems being bought.

summary: A national component [finances awareness, device access and digital culture](2023-04-18-pafen-acces-et-inclusion-numeriques) with no population baseline, instrument or numeric target stated.
developments:
[The national digital-inclusion component finances activities to raise awareness, increase access to broadband-capable devices and develop digital culture, targeting rural communities, women and girls, and vulnerable groups](2023-04-18-pafen-acces-et-inclusion-numeriques). It states no population digital-literacy baseline, no measurement instrument and no numeric target.

That is the whole of the record. A programme with no baseline cannot report progress, and nothing else in the base measures population digital literacy — so the indicator is answered by a description of intent, and will stay that way until something counts.

summary: [49 central-school computer centres were equipped against a 760 target](2024-03-29-menrs-atelier-tics-conditions-apprentissage); a first open-educational-resources strategy [was validated in April 2026](2026-04-16-menrs-validation-strategie-nationale-ressources-educatives-libres).
developments:
[The education ministry's own figure is 49 central-school computer centres equipped and all functional, against a stated target of 760 school networks](2024-03-29-menrs-atelier-tics-conditions-apprentissage) — the clearest measure of the gap on this ledger, and it is the ministry's own.

2026-04-15 to 16 — [a first national strategy on open educational resources was validated by acclamation, giving the country a framework for producing and distributing digital teaching materials across the fondamental and post-fondamental system](2026-04-16-menrs-validation-strategie-nationale-ressources-educatives-libres), framed as digitising accumulated physical materials.

2026-08-11 — [a request for proposals opened for 585 computers and uninterruptible power supplies across 39 central schools in three former provinces](2026-08-11-unicef-rfp-equipements-informatiques-39-ecoles-centrales). Against 760, thirty-nine schools is the increment the window records.

summary: Vietnamese cooperation [delivered 50 desktop computer sets and Master's scholarships in computer science](2026-07-28-burundi-vietnam-digital-transformation-cooperation), against scholarships previously offered and undelivered.
developments:
2026-07-28 — [50 desktop computer sets and Master's scholarships in computer science were reported delivered under the Vietnamese cooperation](2026-07-28-burundi-vietnam-digital-transformation-cooperation), against a starting position in which scholarships of up to US$10,000 each had been offered with nothing delivered on record.

It is the only tertiary provision on this ledger, and it is fifty machines and a handful of places abroad. No university department, laboratory, qualification or graduate count is recorded for the country, and the artificial-intelligence strategy's target of training more than a thousand officials has no programme behind it on the record.

summary: [203 computing-engineering graduates entered the labour market since 2018-2019, with 347 students enrolled in 2023-2024](2024-03-29-menrs-atelier-tics-conditions-apprentissage).
developments:
[The higher teacher-training school put 203 computing-engineering graduates on the labour market since 2018-2019, with 347 students in the computing sections in 2023-2024, 31 per cent of them women](2024-03-29-menrs-atelier-tics-conditions-apprentissage). It is the only supply-side count the base holds and it covers one institution.

2026-03-16 — [a second national coding camp under a continental girls' coding initiative opened for girls selected from across the country, running to 30 March, in programming, digital innovation and leadership, explicitly to prepare them for the digital economy](2026-03-16-onu-burundi-camp-de-codage-filles-agcci-iii), implemented with three ministries.

What neither carries is a destination: no placement rate, no count of graduates working in the sector, and no employer-side demand figure to read the 203 against.

summary: A first documented research workshop [drew university lecturers, doctors, developers and students](2026-07-27-burundi-abadaad-ai-governance-data-ethics-workshop), with no funded programme behind it.
developments:
2026-07-27 — [the first documented workshop on artificial intelligence and data drew university lecturers, doctors, developers and students](2026-07-27-burundi-abadaad-ai-governance-data-ethics-workshop). No baseline was held and no funded programme, research centre or academic department is named.

One convening by an alumni association is the whole of the country's research contribution to digital policy on this ledger. The national strategy's education and research pillar names no institution, and no university programme, publication or advisory body appears anywhere for the country.

summary: A harmonised national complaints strategy [was validated during 2025](2026-02-03-abp-rapport-ombudsman-2025-strategie-gestion-plaintes) and [digital reporting platforms for gender-based violence were presented in April 2026](2026-04-16-abp-lancement-plateformes-digitales-vbg-burundi).
developments:
[The regulator's free short code and physical suggestion boxes in operator agencies are the standing official feedback channel, and they are sectoral: telecoms consumers rather than a cross-government grievance route](2024-01-01-arct-burundi-sensibilisation-doleances-151).

2026-02 — [a harmonised national complaints-management strategy was drawn up and validated during 2025, alongside the ombudsman's 2025 caseload of 776 files analysed and treated](2026-02-03-abp-rapport-ombudsman-2025-strategie-gestion-plaintes).

2026-04-09 — [a citizen-facing digital alert and case-management system for gender-based violence was presented, with an interventions-management system for the institutions involved](2026-04-16-abp-lancement-plateformes-digitales-vbg-burundi). It is the first citizen-facing reporting platform the base holds for Burundi, and it is one subject: no general-purpose portal exists.

summary: An [open online consultation ran on a donor partnership framework](2026-04-21-banque-mondiale-consultations-cpp-burundi-2026-2031), and [a data governance strategy was validated with public, private and civil-society actors](2025-11-06-uneca-burundi-validates-national-data-governance-strategy).
developments:
[The communal administration statute is the founding basis for participation: open communal meetings, consultation of the base for the communal development plan, and hill and quarter development committees](2014-11-28-burundi-loi-1-33-organisation-administration-communale).

2025-11-06 to 07 — [a national validation workshop for the first data governance strategy followed a stakeholder engagement workshop that brought public, private and civil-society actors together to identify priorities](2025-11-06-uneca-burundi-validates-national-data-governance-strategy).

2026-04-21 to 05-05 — [an open online consultation on a donor partnership framework took views from civil-society organisations, non-governmental organisations, the private sector, academia and the media](2026-04-21-banque-mondiale-consultations-cpp-burundi-2026-2031). It is the clearest instance in the window of an online consultation channel addressed to Burundians — and it was opened by an external body rather than by government.

summary: A national survey [is the standing sex-disaggregated measure of access to financial and digital services](2025-06-01-burundi-enquete-nationale-inclusion-financiere-enif-2024); [digital platforms against gender-based violence were built](2026-04-16-abp-lancement-plateformes-digitales-vbg-burundi).
developments:
[The national financial inclusion survey is the standing sex-disaggregated measure of access to financial and digital financial services in Burundi](2025-06-01-burundi-enquete-nationale-inclusion-financiere-enif-2024), and the only recurring gender-disaggregated series the base holds on this subject.

2026-04-09 — [the responsible ministry and a UN agency presented digital platforms built under a national gender-based-violence observatory project: a citizen-facing alert and case-management system through which victims report and are referred for assistance, plus an interventions-management system for the institutions involved](2026-04-16-abp-lancement-plateformes-digitales-vbg-burundi), funded by the European Union.

What is absent is any sex-disaggregated measure of digital access itself — of device ownership, internet use or digital skills — so gender equity is read here through financial services and through a violence-reporting tool rather than through the technology.

progress: No change, a first statement of position with no earlier account behind it
summary: The state's [initial report to the disability rights committee](2025-10-10-burundi-rapport-initial-crpd-c-bdi-1) sets out the statute, the policy, the national committee and the gaps in access to information technology.
developments:
[Burundi's initial report under the disability rights convention is the state's own comprehensive statement of position: ratification, the 2018 statute promoting and protecting the rights of persons with disabilities, the 2020-2024 national policy, the national committee, assistive devices, census data, and the gaps in access to services and to information and communication technology](2025-10-10-burundi-rapport-initial-crpd-c-bdi-1).

It is a baseline and it is the state's own account, submitted nine years after it was due. Nothing else in the base measures digital accessibility: no website accessibility standard, no assistive-technology provision figure and no disaggregated access measure is held, so the position can be described and not tracked.

summary: [Level-2 biometric registration of 54,343 Congolese refugees was completed at one site](2026-07-06-onpra-hcr-enregistrement-biometrique-refugies-congolais-busuma), and cash transfers [reached refugees over their own phones](2025-09-22-sos-medias-burundi-fin-merankabandi-transferts-monetaires-refugies).
developments:
[Asylum claims are recorded in an international agency database and claimants enrolled with fingerprint and iris biometrics, with a refugee identity card issued under the 2021 migration law](2024-02-01-unhcr-burundi-demander-asile-enregistrement-progres-bims) — a registration system operated jointly by the national office and the agency.

2025-09 — [a cash-transfer programme run by government, the World Bank and the food agency closed in one province after two years, having paid 73,600 BIF every two months over recipients' own mobile phones](2025-09-22-sos-medias-burundi-fin-merankabandi-transferts-monetaires-refugies).

2026-07-06 — [level-2 biometric registration of 54,343 Congolese refugees was completed at one site, stated as strengthening protection, improving data quality and better targeting assistance](2026-07-06-onpra-hcr-enregistrement-biometrique-refugies-congolais-busuma). The refugee population is more completely biometrically enrolled than the citizen population, which is the structural fact this indicator keeps recording.

progress: Advanced, on a target rather than on an achieved figure
summary: The broadband programme [targets 80% territorial coverage](2026-05-01-internet-haut-debit-pafen-couvrir-80-du-territoire) and carries a digital villages component, with no achieved figure on file.
developments:
2026-05-01 — [the broadband programme is stated to target 80% of the territory](2026-05-01-internet-haut-debit-pafen-couvrir-80-du-territoire), with [a digital villages component under way and no completion date or coverage achieved on file](2026-05-01-internet-haut-debit-pafen-couvrir-80-du-territoire). No baseline was held for either.

What is measurable sits elsewhere in this report and cuts the other way: tariffs more than doubled, the satellite alternative costs more than most can pay, and the regulator says the network fails mainly on electricity. A territorial coverage target says where a signal reaches; none of the three says whether anyone can afford or rely on it.

summary: A third-generation strategy is in force and [its mid-term evaluation was reported to the statutory sector group in July 2026](2026-08-04-insbu-actualites-et-evenements).
developments:
[The 2022 decree replacing the former institute with the national statistical authority charges its coordination department with elaborating and coordinating implementation of the national strategy for the development of statistics](2022-11-16-decret-100-153-insbu-autorite-statistique-nationale) — the mandate in national law rather than in donor commentary.

2026-05-08 — [a validation workshop was held for the national statistical system's communication and dissemination strategy, aligned to regional guidelines](2026-05-08-le-renouveau-insbu-validation-strategie-communication-ssn).

2026-07-28 — [the statutory sector statistics group met with the recommendations of the third strategy's mid-term evaluation on its agenda](2026-08-04-insbu-actualites-et-evenements), establishing both that a third-generation strategy is in force and that its mid-term evaluation has reported. Neither the strategy nor the evaluation is published, so the base can date the process and not read its findings.

summary: The 2024 census [published preliminary results by decree, enumerating 12,332,788 residents](2025-03-27-burundi-decret-100-032-resultats-preliminaires-rgphae-2024), with definitive results still to come.
developments:
Burundi hosted an Equatorial Guinean delegation over 10-16 August 2026 to share its digital census experience under south-south cooperation ([visit](2026-08-28-bdi-gnq-cooperation-sud-sud-recensement-numerique)).

2025-03-27 — [a decree published the preliminary results of the 2024 census for all purposes pending definitive results: 12,332,788 residents, 5,901,069 men and 6,431,719 women, with 9,255,195 rural against 3,077,593 urban](2025-03-27-burundi-decret-100-032-resultats-preliminaires-rgphae-2024), [with the tables released by the statistics institute](2025-03-27-bdi-insbu-rgphae-2024-tableaux-resultats). The base's prior population figure was a projection off the 2008 enumeration.

Definitive results have not followed in the seventeen months since, and the results are reported against the five provinces created by the 2023 territorial reform rather than the eighteen that preceded them, which breaks comparison with everything published before.

No household survey, no statistics law and no national strategy for the development of statistics appears on this ledger.

summary: Two further sectoral yearbooks were published in the window, one [from the annual school census](2025-12-01-menrs-annuaire-statistique-education-2024-2025-tome-2) and one [built from a ministry's own records](2026-01-01-mctit-annuaire-statistique-edition-2024).
developments:
[The national statistical yearbook is described by the institute itself as a compilation, centralising figures otherwise dispersed across specialised publications and ministry annual reports](2024-12-01-insbu-annuaire-statistique-du-burundi-edition-2023) — which is the administrative-data chain stated in the institute's own words.

2025-12 — [an education yearbook was published for the 2024-2025 school year, produced from the annual school census](2025-12-01-menrs-annuaire-statistique-education-2024-2025-tome-2), the clearest working example of official statistics drawn from an administrative source.

2026-01 — [a trade, transport, industry and tourism yearbook was published, built entirely from the ministry's own administrative records: licences and permits issued, certificates of origin, import-export codes, port and airport traffic and technical-control certificates](2026-01-01-mctit-annuaire-statistique-edition-2024). Three yearbooks and no register-based statistics: the chain runs from paper forms to a book, not from a database to a series.

progress: No change, a first record of the licence with no earlier position behind it
summary: The statistics institute [publishes an open licence permitting reuse, redistribution and derivative products, subject to attribution](2025-06-10-insbu-accord-de-licence-ouverte-plateforme-donnees-ouvertes).
developments:
[The institute's open data platform carries a worldwide, free, non-exclusive licence to use, copy, modify, translate, publish, adapt, distribute and build derivative and value-added products from the data, for commercial and non-commercial purposes, subject to attribution](2025-06-10-insbu-accord-de-licence-ouverte-plateforme-donnees-ouvertes).

It is Burundi's operative open data licence and it is the whole of what the base holds on open data: one institution's platform, with no whole-of-government portal, no publication schedule, no dataset count and no measure of reuse. The page carries no date, so even the licence's age is a proxy from an archived capture.

summary: The national mapping producer [names agriculture among the four purposes of Burundian cartography](2026-08-28-igebu-service-de-cartographie), and census mapping [was cleaned using satellite imagery](2026-02-09-aco-burundi-cartographie-censitaire-apurement-base-rgphae).
developments:
[The national mapping producer's own service page names agriculture as one of the four things Burundian cartography exists to do — identifying and managing agricultural, urban and protected areas — and states that mapping has modernised through remote sensing, satellite positioning, geographic information systems and drones, with a bilateral partnership updating two cities since 2009](2026-08-28-igebu-service-de-cartographie).

2026-02-09 — [the census bureau opened a twenty-day workshop with the mapping institute to clean, verify and update the census cartography database, geoprocessing vector data and interpreting satellite imagery over administrative boundaries covering 3,044 collines et quartiers](2026-02-09-aco-burundi-cartographie-censitaire-apurement-base-rgphae).

The satellite use is real and it is cartographic. No crop-monitoring, yield-estimation or agricultural early-warning product built on satellite data is held.

summary: A satellite imagery viewer [publishes named geostationary layers on automatic update](2026-08-28-igebu-images-satellitaires-calques-dynamiques), and [impact-based forecasting was launched in May 2026](2026-05-27-igebu-atelier-lancement-previsions-basees-sur-les-impacts-wiser).
developments:
2025-09 — [the automatic weather station network was connected to the international data exchange system for the first time, moving off the older network and beginning international transmission, including a backlog archived since 2022 that had sat unexploited on local servers](2025-09-04-igebu-echange-international-de-donnees-wis2). The same account is candid about why the network had been down: expired SIM cards, unpaid data plans and lack of basic maintenance.

2026-05-27 to 29 — [impact-based forecasting was launched with the world meteorological organisation, to turn meteorological data into decision-ready information](2026-05-27-igebu-atelier-lancement-previsions-basees-sur-les-impacts-wiser), a capability launch and staff training rather than a delivered product.

[The institute publishes a satellite imagery viewer whose named dynamic layers are geostationary precipitation, infrared and convection products, plus natural-colour imagery and a cloud mask, on automatic update](2026-08-28-igebu-images-satellitaires-calques-dynamiques).

summary: A five-year United States health-sector agreement [commits US$156m and includes health-data management](2026-02-09-us-commits-156m-burundi-health-sector-agreement); no data-sharing agreement under it is published.
developments:
2026-02-09 — [a five-year memorandum with the United States committing US$156m to the health sector was signed, including health-data management](2026-02-09-us-commits-156m-burundi-health-sector-agreement), where nothing existed before.

It is the only United States engagement on this ledger and the largest foreign commitment of any origin. No data-sharing agreement under it has been published, no implementing arrangement is named, and no disbursement has been reported in the six months since. No hyperscaler, cloud provider or American technology vendor appears anywhere in the record for the country.

summary: A framework agreement [was signed whose stated object is digital transformation of the mining chain](2026-07-03-ibi-burundi-mining-authority-comprehensive-mining-cooperation-agreement), and [equipment was handed to the state news agency](2026-06-02-abp-ambassade-de-chine-offre-materiel-de-travail-abp).
developments:
[A satellite television project was handed over with 300 villages equipped, implementing a continental forum pledge and funded through a south-south cooperation fund](2019-03-11-cidca-chinese-government-funded-satellite-tv-project-burundi) — the most nearly primary record of a Chinese digital commitment to Burundi being delivered.

2026-05-28 — [the ambassador visited the state news agency and handed over information technology and production equipment](2026-06-02-abp-ambassade-de-chine-offre-materiel-de-travail-abp). Small in value, and the only Chinese digital or media-technology engagement in the window recorded by a Burundian official source.

2026-07 — [a framework agreement was signed whose stated object is explicitly digital: digital transformation of the whole mining industry chain, data-driven exploration and detection technology, laboratory capacity and a digital platform connecting resources to markets](2026-07-03-ibi-burundi-mining-authority-comprehensive-mining-cooperation-agreement). No text of any China-Burundi digital memorandum is publicly held, so the substance is known through the counterparty's own account.

summary: A regional digital economy programme [formally started covering Burundi](2026-06-24-eac-2026-digital-for-development-forum-eu-eac-deep), and [three digital tools were handed to a ministry](2026-07-14-onu-femmes-ue-burundi-remise-plateformes-numeriques-vbg), against [no bilateral digital priority](2021-12-21-ue-programme-indicatif-multiannuel-2021-2027-burundi).
developments:
[The bilateral programming instrument carries no standalone digital or data priority area for Burundi; digital appears transversally across the three priority areas](2021-12-21-ue-programme-indicatif-multiannuel-2021-2027-burundi) — a negative finding, and the frame everything else here sits in.

2026-06-24 — [a forum marked the formal start of a co-financed regional digital economy programme covering Burundi as one of eight partner states: digital transformation strategy, e-commerce, interoperable cross-border payments, e-government and cybersecurity](2026-06-24-eac-2026-digital-for-development-forum-eu-eac-deep). It is the most concrete European digital commitment reaching Burundi, and it reaches it regionally rather than bilaterally.

2026-07-14 — [three digital tools were formally handed to the responsible ministry through a UN agency, with a vehicle, seventeen motorcycles and training for 47 officials and 13 managers](2026-07-14-onu-femmes-ue-burundi-remise-plateformes-numeriques-vbg).

progress: No change, one announced intention and no instrument
summary: One engagement is documented: [a Qatari holding group announcing intended investment in cybersecurity, digital transformation and telecommunications](2025-08-17-presidence-burundi-partenariat-qatar-al-massour-holding).
developments:
[The President received a Qatari delegation from a holding group, which announced intended investment in cybersecurity, digital transformation, telecommunications and banking](2025-08-17-presidence-burundi-partenariat-qatar-al-massour-holding).

That is the only documented Gulf digital or data engagement the base holds, and the finding beside it is the more useful one: no Gulf-Burundi memorandum, framework agreement or loan specifically on digital or data was located. An announced intention by a private group, received at the presidency, is what stands in for a bilateral relationship here — no instrument, no value and no follow-up is on the record.

summary: Talks opened [on adapting an India Stack-style identity linked to instant payments](2026-06-30-burundi-india-stack-digital-id-payments-biometricupdate), with nothing signed.
developments:
2026-06-23 — [talks opened on adapting the Indian digital public infrastructure model, an Aadhaar-style identity linked to instant payments](2026-06-23-burundi-studies-india-stack-digital-id-payments), [reported again a week later](2026-06-30-burundi-india-stack-digital-id-payments-biometricupdate) and [as a partnership on digital identity](2026-06-26-burundi-india-partnership-digital-identity-techafricanews). Nothing has been signed.

The fit is closer than most such talks: the country has an instant payment system live since April 2026 and a biometric identity card technically ready and waiting on its instrument, which are the two halves the model joins. No memorandum, technical assistance agreement or timetable has followed.
